Derwent obeys, and puts his joke away. He’s not an overtly rude student. Anyway, he’ll tell it later. In truth the teacher knows she has to reprimand him, but because he’s the funniest person in class she’s secretly disappointed that she can’t listen-in on the joke as well.

Des is the name of a dust-covered Rolls Royce motorcar that’s been sitting in an uncle’s garage for nearly 20 years. No one is certain, of course, but there is a popular perception that if he was ever to wake from his slumber he would be a marvellous and reliable individual.
Married to Ethel.

The world’s most gifted car mechanic. He’s damn-near telepathic, he admits to having performed more than 200 burnouts in his life and he speaks and deals with only the truth. “Hey,” he says, on the morning of the 25th of December, hungover from the night before, and ready to go again. “Merry Christmas....fucking!”

Dev is a cracker. As a busy optimist with a big smile he’s anything but lazy. He’s a great dancer, sports a large group of friends, arrives into romance easily and he treats his ladies and lovers well. Colourful shirts are his trademark.
Devin seems to cram a lot into a small space. Always thinking, he dislikes waste, be it something in a moment or on his plate, he's never late and he does what he says he's going to do.
See Alexandra.

Rarely lacking self-confidence and ambition, Dex is one of those people who, once they realise what it is they want to achieve, sets out a strategic plan which is not only well-thought out and logical, but is usually good for those around him. He never blows his own horn for the sake of attention and he doesn’t appreciate those who do. Having said all that, he’s not as serious as all this sounds, either. Indeed, to many, Dex is something of an enigma and all we can suggest is that you take some time and go discover Dex’s depths properly.
The Swindler, The Joker, The Partier, etc etc.

No, not diablo, he's not the devil, it's Diallo; like yellow after you wake up half asleep and forgetful. Is he a little dreamy in his approach? Well, probably yes, but only because a secret little part of his name, right before the l's, tries to disarm you by putting you to sleep. Nothing is taken too seriously in this court ladies and gentlemen, and because he's not stupid he tends to arrive where he aims. Not bad, really. But don't ask us what he does for a living, although he'd benefit from doing something near or in the ocean. Good luck.
The informal name hides the formal nature of the fellow. Mr. Cool, Mr. Deceptively Competitive and Mr. Genuine Nice Guy, he is. And he has a sense of humour. (It’s the only obvious part about him.)
A normal fellow (he isn’t) who is in possession of a rapier wit. There were rumours that he once wore loud shirts and sported a short mans’ syndrome, but this theory has been subsequently debunked.
Exotic and eccentric, Didier rarely follows a well-trodden path. Friendly and honest, he always sees beyond the facade and his jokes and insights, therefore, are beyond many. Thank Christ.
Diego, you ain’t no hound dog, so stand up and be counted, boy!
Detached and inert when he needs to be, and sometimes when even when he doesn’t, Diesel is one of the most determined individuals in the entire Kingdom.

Diet is dogmatic to the point of irritation. But, we, as a society of apathetic, lazy humans need him in case we ever decide to get off our arses and help. So, keep at it Diet and don't listen to the complaints. Management.

Mmm, you might imagine Dietmar to be a strict task master and someone without a sense of humour. After all, not many German-sounding names lend themselves to visions of high comedy, but Dietmar is something of an exception. Sure, he's a bit serious around the dinner table - I mean, you can't just pick up a bone in your hands and eat it - but mostly he looks for silly situations and odd people to amuse him. He's a bit silly himself, you see. Dietmar.
Digby has huge ears like Babaar the elephant. They turn red when he gets excited and if he’s really excited they start flapping.
A pesky little bastard with a lightning sense of humour who can multi-task better than most men. He’s always on the look-out.
Dimitri’s first reaction to people he doesn’t know is one of utter warmth.

Is he Indian or Arabic, or maybe Persian? No one is quite sure, but my goodness, just have a look at him will you? He’s smooth. He’s patient. And he carries a certain kind of humorous grace that soothes. Nice work Dinesh.

“Racing now and they burst from the blocks, drinking, drinking, drinking. Four rounds in and it’s Ding leading Ryan by a short half head. Touch and go as they make the final push for home. Empty glasses, tears and spittle cover the table and it’s a sad and sorry sight. LOOK OUT! A BRAWL HAS ERUPTED! YES, IT’S DING IN THE MIDDLE OF IT! He’s bleeding but he doesn’t seem to care and, yes, Ding prevails by half a length! Oooh, geeez, his head is going to hurt tomorrow, Brian, don’t you think?”
“Oh my word, yes, George. Well called. Tomorrow is not going to be a fun day for these boys.”
Indeed.
Ding, mate, get yourself an off switch. It might save your life one day.
First to arrive at the party and last to leave, Dinga sobs when his sporting team loses and he loves his tats. His version of foreplay involves him asking the question, “Honey, feel like a tickle?”

Option A: Another Kiwi (what are they doing here?). His idea of the perfect meal is a special kind of slop that involves making a soup of mash potato containing at least one can of carnation milk, into which are dropped two or three lamb chops that have been incinerated to within an inch of their lives. Like his personality as a whole, the entire thing is borderline-carcinogenic.

Option B: Australian. Quick on his feet and he never looks back for too long. Dingo is certainly present. He’s silly but not stupid, kinky but not arrestable, and he’s a better lateral thinker than a skilled CIA operative, and certainly funnier.

Man, he's slippery. He's vanished from so many girls' morning bedrooms it isn't funny. Smart, with an excellent memory, Dino did eventually grow up. Yes, he can commit now, but he'll always be young at heart.
The IT guy.
Dirk is the only man in the animal kingdom who has willingly super-glued both of his hands to his own cock.

Yes, Dirty is a cheeky bastard who, in his younger days, involved himself in all manner of dare-devil escapades. From the outside the risks he took were substantial, but Dirty is no fool - not now not then - and so they were always calculated and he was never in genuine peril…..we’re pretty sure. These days he’s actually quite responsible. Crazy eh?
Commitment phobe.
Drummer.
Doc is super smart and possesses a photographic memory but he has very little common sense.

A rolling stone gathers no moss and Dom is at least that, then some. Friends and laughter fill his life and romance is never really an issue for such a positive soul. An intelligent cat who travels and experiments, Dom will be searching for the good times and the good people so long as he is able. Work-wise, he’ll lead bands, companies and work crews, always with a smile, and he can be a kinky fucker as well. Splendid work Dom.

Domenico - is he pig-headed?
Yep.
Is he funny?
Yep.
Is he broke?
Not usually.
Will he see a project through to the end?
If it’s worthy, yes.

Dominic is passionate to the point of being lethal. He’s the sort of man, who, if he took to the back of a horse for the first time whilst in love and enraptured with the moment in general, may very well ride the animal to its death.
A council worker’s shovel. He holds a lot of dirt and doesn’t mind grovelling in mud one iota. In fact he enjoys it.

(Can we disregard that American President? He simply doesn't count as a fully compassionate, intelligent and friendly human.) Anyway, outside any kind of political jurisdiction Donald is like a donkey. Presuming he isn't either completely brainwashed or incredibly narrow-minded, he walks slowly, whether he’s carrying much weight or not, and he doesn’t understand why something like the pyramids generates all the fuss that they do. Donald is simple man and the good Donalds are humble farmers. These fellows are doing the best they can with the tools they possess, and they're considerate.

All that make sense?...

As a sufferer of the middle-child syndrome Donni has a temper and he can be selfish. But, Donni, forget all that for a minute. You do know that if you keep this mini-crime thing going it's only a matter of time before you get arrested or beaten up?

Option A: Donny is in jail and he’s one of those prisoners who is liked by everyone, inmates and guards alike. 

Option B: Donny is that old bloke at the football club, without whom the place would fall apart. Who would go out and collect the footballs left alone on the ground after training is over? Who would turn off all the lights and lock up the sheds? Who would make sure there were enough oranges for the team on game day? And he knows the name of every player. 
And he asks for very little. (Maybe remember that come Christmas time.)
His wardrobe consists only of Polo Ralph Lauren shirts with the gay polo player on the front. He aspires to be a sports reader on the TV news.
Let's his friends make the decisions.

Doogan lives in a house surrounded by rainforest. He spends most of his time in the nude, he eats his own vegetables and a myriad of birds and parrots call his house and garden home. Peace, love and contentment are Doogan's emotional companions and it's a wonderful thing. His car is held together with rust and humour.
The man in control of the stash.

Doone is a fascinating creature. Over time he has evolved special receptors in his brain that have attuned his senses to the movements of rock within the earth’s crust, which is only one of his many eccentricities.
Doover snaps his fingers, even while doing something as banal as making a cup of tea.

No one is as cluey as Oscar Wilde, Dorian, and neither are you. (Are you tired of the references?) Anyway, Dorian is intelligent, he is subdued sometimes although his ego, when it turns up, is hard to suppress or ignore. Keep an eye on that, eh chief? University educated, Dorian is never destined for the cues at the unemployment shop.
The name of the great moose head that’s hanging on the wall. He’s great to talk to when you come home, pissed as a mute.
(No description needed.) Everybody....I’d like you to meet Dougal!
"Here, give me that you bloody weakling," he barks, calling for the larger sledge hammer. Douglas.

Doyle strictly adheres to the rules of engagement which exist inside and between families of means. Tradition is important here and Doyle, despite his easy nature, agrees wholeheartedly. Fucking boring if you ask me, then again I’m not lining myself up for a $12 million inheritance.

Originally from Nepal and originally named Nitten Redicum Bak Bak, Dream is the sort of fellow, who, when standing in the light of a roaring bonfire, rolling a cigarette and quietly swaying to music of the party, will elicit a sudden and instinctive scream of, “DREEEEEEEEEAAM!!”, from the two desperados sitting down, nearby, who have simultaneously spotted him, and who have given up any hope of finding anybody with a lighter. We’re lucky to have him.

Thoughtful. Quiet. Measured…at least, this is what people were led to believe. Perhaps he simply has no desire to be seen or heard by people he has no time for? Either way Drew is a meticulous planner and splendid fun.
Drex found God in a permaculture garden.

Dries walks tall and talks directly at you. Confrontation is a trifle for this fellow, although if he has any South African blood in him then it’s almost a given. He’s never going to be homeless, unless of course he gets tired of it all and decides to spend a few years living out there alone on the African Savanna eating the natives. Is he a wanker? Well, not with a rifle in his hand, no.

As soon as his (Israeli) government told him he had to join the army and, in all likelihood, try and shoot someone, that was it. He left the country, threw his passport out and wound up in either Byron Bay, Australia, or Varanasi, India, selling herbs at a specialist 'herb shop'. Funny as hell, Dror hasn't got an angry bone in his body.

Dru is far from a boring accountant. If he's partying, and he tends to do that very well, you can expect to see him in psychedelic clothing which looks the same whether you've ingested an acid tab or not. He tends to get bored at the drop of a hat so if you intend to marry Dru be mindful of that, although, as a reasonably savvy operator, chances are that he wouldn't select a partner who wasn't suited to him anyway. Know what I mean?

The hidden artist. D.S is constructed of splendid moral fibre that enables him to exercise his substantial talents. From the ground up, he is designed perfectly for whatever it is that he decides to do with his life. And he is one funny individual.

If he wasn't such a decent person you could almost call D-Trye machiavellian in the way he goes about it. In his own way I suppose he is. But he means well, though. Indeed, half the time he's quite mystifying. Like several in the Kingdom however, you don't often see him during the day.
Duane (and his twin brother Dwane) excel at church group, and yes, let's face it, somebody has to, and that's alright.
Wet feet.

A comic genius who doesn’t know it. He still can’t understand why the Queen gave him an Order of the Commonwealth but he forgot all that nonsense when he rushed-off to try and rescue the love of his life. Bravo Dudley! Bravo!!

Rarely blonde, Duds makes his way from space to space very smoothly, as if he’s a pool ball rolling across flat, green velvet. Women seem to be attracted to him easily although even he can’t really tell you how he ends up with these girlfriends. It just kind of happens. In terms of a career, he’s never doing what you’d think he’d be doing. He’s never that straight forward. That make sense?

Some people just manage to land on their feet, no matter how much they’re in debt and no matter how many scars their ex-partners inflict upon them. 
Having said all that, Duke, some advice brother: If you find yourself with a wad of cash in your pocket, some day, don’t piss it up against a wall or bet the lot on a supposedly brilliant stock market tip. Take a few deep breaths and buy a chunk of property somewhere. No, it’s not the most daring thing to do and you’ll never make yourself famous for it, but once in a while you need to keep your feet planted on the ground....then again, maybe this is none of your business. Anyone got any ideas?...

Alright, so he doesn’t have a clue how long it takes for photons of light to travel from the Sun to planet Earth, he has the table manners of a frothing pig and he’s never heard of Bolivia, let alone its capital city, but Dummy is a bona fide legend. Why? Because he is a lover and a fighter who susses people out in a flash – be they good, bad or useless – he always thinks laterally, he is a generous friend and when it comes to women he is a gracious gentlemen.

Option A:  The Solemn Priest. He is at home in front of his brethren. He is at home on the ocean. 

Option B:  The name of Sean’s cock.
Dundee used to work at the crocodile park and he has almost certainly slept with Deidre.
Salt of the Earth.
Duran, if he’s called only that, never suffers from a dreadful dress sense. No way. His shoes are expensive and shiny and he’d rather look good than be broke.

No, Dusan isn't an oaf although he does look kind of oafish. Perhaps it's just because he takes a while to answer. Not because he's daft or anything, he's actually very bright, but he likes to contemplate all possible results, that's all. Dusan.
Polite and reliable, Dustin does a good job of cleaning up the edges.

An unflappable character who rarely looks infuriated, probably because he rarely is. The days keep rolling on in life, and Dusty is very aware of the length and breadth of the whole process, which is why he keeps a steady hand.

Maybe he’s from Holland. Maybe he isn’t. It doesn’t matter. In the same vein as Clarky, Bill, Joe, Graeme, Jack, Jimmy and Bob, Dutchy is here for the stay, for the good times and the bad, he’ll laugh and help when he can, if he can, and in the wash-up all of us are glad that he is around. And when he’s gone we will mourn his absence. Cheers Dutchy.
Dwane (and his twin brother Duane) excel at church group, and let's face it, someone has to.

“Yeah, I’m a great shot,” he’ll say, and the conviction and the intensity with which he says it have you believing him.
Truth is, he’s never picked up a rifle in his life, but sometimes we all need to stave off the inevitable. Dwight would make an excellent permanent political secretary.

Like the rubber grip of a handle for anything that has a handle, Dylan looks okay and provides something for the universe, I suppose. He's quite proud of his hairdo. Indeed, he once crashed his car because he was staring at his reflection in the shop windows as he was driving along. Luckily he wasn't moving fast and the car in front only received minor dents.
Marc's colleague.

The name of a particular colour of paint. He’s not black, he’s not grey and he’s not blue - he’s Eamon, and he pleasantly fills background space without tearing the room to pieces. Is he boring?...Mmm, a little bit.
Earl loves either gridiron, rugby or soccer, he lives for ten pin bowling with his pals every Friday night and he is a gifted hooligan, in general. He wears lots of rings.
Early has clear head and he doesn’t talk shit. He may have had a tough start to life but it has made him tough and true at the finish.

Ignore the brooding good looks and the occasionally cool facade because East is a lovely fellow who simply isn't as outgoing as one might expect him to be. He approaches his career/careers like an old diesel engine which takes ages to get up to speed: in the beginning he stops and coughs and spits abit, but once his revs are up he's a fine specimen. (Note: he's much better off outdoors than in and he's not really the kinky type.)

A lot more volatile than he looks. If no one keeps an eye on Easton he’ll end up off the map. Give him something to do and encourage him in it. He ain’t someone who needs to spend oodles of time inside his own head.

His name curls around itself like a content koala up in a tree. Ever seen one in the wild? You’ll be lucky to see one moving. At best you might see one munching on a gum leaf, but usually they seem to be asleep. They never appear to concern themselves with the future, they definitely don’t concern themselves with the past, and all they appear to deal with is the unfolding present moment, and where their substantive imagination takes them. 
I give you Eckhart.

Closely related to Malcolm, Ed is a huge log that you throw on the fire in the dead of winter. He is a massive awkward thing that takes a while to lumber into place but once he gets going he throws out enough steadying light, heat and humour to warm all but the biggest of rooms. (Serendipity is his close ally although he is a little lazy in bed.)
Full of wisecracks and hair-brain schemes.
See Eddie.
Eden is perfectly centred, he is innovative and he carries a glorious sense of fun. He’d make a good father.
A nice thick piece of cheddar cheese. Pregnant women sometimes crave his company and he often forms the part of many-a-meal that might be described as ‘comfort food’.

Cryptic crosswords and scrabble - I fucking doubt it. Edgy is too busy cave diving. Perhaps he’s ice climbing or snow boarding? Edgy is the sort of fellow who will host a party that is so loud and packed with people the entire house will need re-stumping afterwards.

If he were a chimpanzee, while the rest of his troop swung and hooted and hollered around him, being silly in the moment, Edison would hang pendulous by a single arm, contemplating whatever the equivalent of the chimpanzee money market is. Does that make him boring? Well, perhaps, but we all have a niche to fill.

As Walter’s younger cousin, Edmund says, “Yes dear”, “No dear”, “Sorry dear” and, “Okay dear”, so often that he sometimes says them in his sleep. 
Poor Edmund.

Edward always wears spectacles. As a leading diplomat in the foreign office he spends most of his time placating visiting V.I.Ps who are still offended by the behaviour of some of his embassy staff at the party that was held the night before.

Edwin joined the Navy and became an officer - more for the white uniform than to actually go into battle. However he can only compute only one order at a time and he can’t swim freestyle for more than 35 metres before he starts to inhale water.

Here's a tip: If you're the central umpire adjudicating a game of tennis in which Egor is playing and you make a call that he believes is wrong, you won't hear him yell and scream at you, oh no. But you might have to dodge his racquet currently flying at your head. (And it doesn’t matter if it's a Grand Slam event, or just a 'friendly' Sunday afternoon get-together with a few friends.)

PS- Don't take it personally.

His parents were Swedish politicians, which is one thing, but no one has any idea how to either spell or pronounce his name. The only thing we know for certain is that Einar rhymes with “When do you think your gonna’?”, and to that end he charges at life like a drunk village idiot in a bad mood. Get in his way and you’re basically fucked.
The more complex the game, the better. He's an academic who, like Bernard, has never once changed the oil in any car he has ever owned.
A cross between a gecko, a rainforest and an extroverted hairdresser, Eko and his Indonesian heritage are the perfect example of compassion, good grace and cheeky clean fun.

Elan drives a sports car with tan leather gloves, he wears a white or cream-coloured polo neck jumper that costs at least $800, even when it's not that cold, and he shaves his nuts at least as much as Marco.
Clean fingernails.

(Said very quietly) Now, Elfin, if you can just come this way please and go and speak to those people through there. They'll be able to help you, okay?
(Postscript: Elfin moves to where he is supposed to go, to the room where mental assistance awaits for those who presume they are a character from a movie. We think he’s going to be fine. It might take a while though…)
Graceful, musical and unflustered.
Elian, it might be time to go and break some rules son. Just for the hell of it…

Elias looks relaxed. He’s sitting next to his boss, the CEO, and he can feel his superior’s sudden rush of fear. What was supposed to be an initial, friendly discussion about a possible investment has been turned on its head. Clearly, what these three immaculately dressed visitors have in mind is a hostile takeover. 
The CEO is passed a piece of paper with a number written on it, and he sits there staring at it. Elias flicks a glance sideways and he can sense the fear amid his superior’s indecision. Immediately, Elias leans in to his colleague and suggests they have a quick word outside. 
Out in the foyer Elias whispers quietly, “Fuck those backstabbing mother fuckers. We’ve done too much. We’ve invested too much, and finally we’ve got this place working. We don’t need their money and you know it. Forget what the board thinks John. Let’s go back in there and you tell them to go and get fucked. And if you don’t I will.”
John smiles. He knows Elias is right. He’s always right…
Deeper than you perceive, Eligh would make a wonderful crook because with a face as innocent as his, let alone his capacity to act very well, no one would ever suspect him.
The Rattlesnake, which is to say what you see and hear is rarely the truth.

“Oh no,” Eliot’s wife says to their two kids, handing them the invite to the fancy dress party. “Have a look at this. But quick, I think that's your father in the driveway now.”
Her son reads the card and drops his head with a defeated sigh, while her daughter looks at her mother in a panic and says, “Oh Muuuuuum. Can we just not tell him this time? Pleeeeeeasssssssse? He gets so excited by these things he doesn't even sleep!” And amen to that, young Eliot.

An upstanding man who doesn’t take things too seriously, and overall he’s excellent company. Aside from being highly intelligent, Elliott is also the name of a musical note that’s played on a flute by a man wearing tights.
There's an American air force base named after him, which is fine by him. He's always liked a man in uniform.

It's a relaxing-sounding name, isn't it? Yet a little surprising at the same time too, which is why he's so good to have at sea - the last thing anyone needs in a confined space is an emotional idiot affecting the moral of the whole crew, plus he always keeps you thinking. Indeed, as the world's best racing-yacht tactician Elon is positioned perfectly up there near the helm right next to the skipper, so his directives can be taken up immediately. And chances are, if the skipper does what they're told with the resources available to them, victory will be assured. Nice work Elon.

No, Elroy is never going to make the sacrifices needed to travel to faraway lands, set up a colony and start life afresh on the other side of the planet. He's quick-fix kind of guy. Friends come and go fast in his life because he's never in the same place twice.

Bored at staring up at a black board for nine months and studying things he wasn't that fussed about, by the time exams began he was at the end of his tether, but, he walked into the exam room having studied his fair measure. He sat down, the clock began, 150 students opened their exam booklets and he did the same. Then, in a moment of clarity, quite slowly Elton closed his, took a breath and stood up.
“No. Fuck this. I’ve tried, but I’ve had enough.” Elton.
When all the other parties have petered out on a Friday or Saturday night, everyone heads back to Elvis’s pad and to the one party that will ride it out to the dawn, and possibly the one after.
"Well, howdy, y'all...... My names Elwood. I'm buddies with JD and I really like eatin' cake. Greeeaaaat big piles of cake.......!!! What do you like?...." Even labrador dogs are embarrassed by him.

Austerity measures? No, Elwyn is more into celebratory measures and techniques. Sure, he seems quiet and almost timid but not once you know him. Most of his humour runs far too deep for the average punter on the street.
Focus, is the key, son. FOCUS!
Dark eyebrows. Sympathetic heart.
As another one who is in love with stationary, Emerson rarely gets his hands dirty and is destined for a life and a career indoors. Does he exercise or dance? Let's hope so…

Emery is the captain of most of the school’s sports teams. As a natural (yet non-egotistical) leader, he is sought out for opinion and counsel both on and off the field, and he stands up for his team mates, which is why they adore him. But it can be a double-edged sword. Emery is made of rather strict moral fibre, you see, and whoa-betide any of his chargers who he discovers taking ecstasy the week before the grand final. No matter how good they are and no matter how badly he thinks the team needs them, such an act would result in instant dismissal. As you can imagine, the ladies simply adore him as well.

As a quiet and gentle-mannered man who has a particular kind of relationship with both the stars and some of the four-legged creatures which surround us, Emil should think about getting away from city life where he is often led down sleazy and unhealthy paths. He should think about becoming a goat herder…(It’d do you good, Emil.)
As girl called Gabriela in a past life, Emile is one cool cat. True, and just like Coco, actually, he’s barely ever lifted a shovel but so what? Keep on slidin’ Emile, keep on slidin’…

Like the good-looking wake of a luxury yacht, Emilio trails just behind the chaos with something of a smile, knowing all the hard work has been done by someone else, up ahead. And that's okay. The only trade off is that when a situation gets particularly precarious, confronting or downright ugly, there's a chance he'll take his easy smile and his gentle joie de vivre around the corner and vanish altogether.
Come on rock star, stop talking it up and show us what you've got!

Like is his twin brother with the one m, Emmerson is a modern, technologically-fluent man who doesn’t know the first thing about dirt, worms and permaculture. And that’s okay. In the new era of clean energy, stain-free sheets and well-tended old-growth forests, we’ll need Emmerson in admin to make sure all the apps holding the modern world together are functioning smoothly. 
(Note: If Emmerson is born in South or Central America, Spain or Portugal, we have no fucking idea what he’s up to. He could drive a garbage truck for all we know, although whatever he's doing he’d be funny to sit next to.)

In a past life Emmett hunted alligators in the Florida everglades like you see on one of those stupid bloody television shows. Today in this life he still answers most questions with one syllable if possible, but he’s a whole lot friendlier and smarter, and his personal hygiene has improved through the roof. Peace out Emmett.

Have you ever noticed how some people just seem to have more time than others? It's weird. Ennio is the sort of fellow who doesn’t need to mediate because he unwittingly mediates all the time, just by breathing in and out, deeply and slowly. He'd make a gifted free diver and probably break all sorts of records, and here on land it endears him with a wonderful sense of calm which is wholly infectious. What's he doing these days? Who cares. He's happy and he's at peace, and so are those around him. Amen to that, young Ennio.

In Spain he might as well be called Shane – who knows – but here, he’s a potent ball of energy that, like several of his peers, lives for the sight of girls’ knickers. And he generally gets to see plenty.

Option A: Oh look, go and watch the movie The Big Blue. It'll save everyone time.

Option B: A large male poodle who knows his photo is being taken, and who will pose accordingly. In that regard he is identical to his human brother.

Eric is a light-hearted Goat and one of the Gifted Ones in that he is the luckiest being in the entire Kingdom. Outstanding effort, Eric. (Okay, okay, so some Erics are incredibly lazy and make useless husbands, not that he’s ever aware of that.)
As a palaeontologist of some note, Erich is very excited by shovels and brushes, not to mention canvas sock protectors.

The academic with a very dry sense of humour. He's often so engrossed in his studies/projects that if you passed him in the corridor and said hello he'd barely notice you were there, let alone respond. Don't take it personally.
Another Arts student. Erin wears $420 shirts and aches to resemble one of those dopy male models in a magazine ad for Christ-knows-what.

What Ernan would never do is allow any of the machines that he owns to fall into a state of disrepair. Car, truck, lawn mower or chainsaw, and especially the electric winch that he built himself to haul buckets of water up from the dam, Ernan keeps a close eye on all his gadgets. I shudder to think what he gets up to in bed.
The name of an old country homestead that sits on a rich pastoralist’s property. Quiet, calm and cool in the heat of the summer, he battens down the hatches in winter and hibernates.

Ernesto has charisma, and he has no issues around declaring bankruptcy. If things are good then great, he’ll live large and hold up a candle to the good times and he’ll foot the bill. But at the first sign of an inevitable storm he’s out the back door as quick as a heated tomcat and fuck the consequences about angry creditors who have been left in the lurch. No storm = no trouble. His personal life is therefore more dramatic than most.

Yeah, yeah, he’s heard the Benny Hill jokes. Forget all that for a tic. Ernie is loving and compassionate, and sure, he’ll never fully grow up, but perhaps that means he ism already because aren’t highly evolved souls the best at playing in this moment?

Perhaps we need to ship Errin off to Palestine, then Syria, then Afghanistan, then Chechnya, then basically anywhere large groups of people are in conflict? You see, Errin is a peaceful man who exudes calm, and who encourages one to contemplate their inner-turmoils. Forgiveness: he accidentally promotes this without even meaning to. Weird, eh? But don’t presume by all this that he represents a serious man. He's not, he's just young at heart.
A Fiat Bambino 500 motorcar. Forget Herbie the Clint, Errol has style and panache, and he makes others laugh by simply looking at him.

Erwin is a peculiar man. Because he is supremely dogmatic he is well-suited to his profession of an investigative reporter. He's been threatened with the sack so often from the chief editor that it doesn't even register anymore. Like a tenacious Jack Russell with his eye on the truth, Erwin will persist, and ask, and probe until he finds the REAL STORY. And he's great at feigning igronance if he's over-spent his budget.

Oh dear, once again we find a set of parents who’s own parents required a decent education. What is one to do? Anyway, here is Essex, a young man (and grandson) named-so in the hope he will be propelled into a cool and unique setting (personality) and where fame and fortune await. 

(Private Message from Management to Essex: Essex, brother, beware the fools in your midst. Their sense of self-worth is not great, and this is a potential vacuum which, without an eye to the outside greater world, might suck you down with it. You with me? …..good. So, have some fun then get out. It’s a big, wonderful world and you will do well in and upon it. Amen.)
E.T simply can't belieeeeeeeve how good he looks. And he's a happy man.

“Eee – than” rhymes with “Not – fair”. As a serious young man who lacks the ability to grow any kind of facial hair, the only avenue for Ethan to look older or serious, therefore, is to frown constantly. But dont let that dissuade you. Ethan is a lovely, gentle fellow.

Ethen has slightly less time to waste than his twin brother, Ethan, which means he gets to places faster in lieu of spending less time thinking about how and where he is going. Still, there is some uncertainty about where he really wants to be and why. Is this why he looks quite serious, usually?

Etienne wears scarves in his hair and a myriad of thin, multi-coloured leather bracelets on his wrist. Travelled, yes, French, probably, either in this life or a recent past one, and he wields a massive depth of interest in those who have experienced a different life history to his, which, let’s face it, is most people. Etienne isn’t a hard man, but he tries hard at being loving and optimistic. That makes him tough enough in anyone’s language. Etienne, the feathers in your hair look ridiculous but we don’t care. We’re just glad you're around.

Like a fine aged wine, Euan is in for the long haul. He takes no shortcuts and he’s very much about the journey. He does what he says, he’s mild-mannered and he is the one of the most patient people you will ever meet.

For an unusual name Eugene is just a normal sort of bloke, and a nice one. (Note: The thing about Eugene is that, though his name begins oddly, it quite quickly becomes an unexpectedly smooth ride over rolling green hills.)
Ev is one of the good guys. He’s open in dealings, he’s friendly in company, he enjoys kids and strangers and he helps out. Barely a bad word ever gets said about him, and rightly so.

It doesn’t happen much these days because the world’s gone to CDs and beyond but once upon a time vinyl records were all the rage and sometimes they received scratches, and every time the needle ran over one it would skip. “Evan…Evan…Evan..,” the speakers would blurt, and you’d drop your head at another album destroyed. (Yes, Evan is hyper-organised and no one wishes that he wasn’t. Amen.)
Boy, was he barked at a lot. Let’s hope he gets “Ev” or “Evo”, otherwise he’s going to plod along in the guise of a rather staid, conservative and ostensibly boring individual.

Well, at least they didn't call you K2. That'd be flat out silly now, wouldn't it? As it happens, Everest isn't the mountain we were led to believe, but he's a decent person. And yes, once again we see parents drunk in front of an atlas trying to name a child - what do you do?

A pulsating individual who has done it all. A huge smile on his face is always a good start, but Evo is traipsing through life as if charging through virgin jungle with a machete, and he’s had a few of those too. Was he a stripper for a while or am I making that up? Last I heard he was setting up a surfing backpackers in Ecuador, but that was a while back. Perhaps they made a TV show about him? Is he still alive?….

You can’t help but contort the inside of your throat to say it, but somehow he manages to pull-off a great comeback. Regardless of that, Ewan is a nice guy and a skilled carpenter who is as good with his hands as he is with his repartee.
See Ewan.

Exavier is too polite to be particularly manly. But, he did well at school and he’ll probably do well at university if he attends. He was never going to be a plumber. He's not quick witted enough for a start.

Option A: The gifted yoga Instructor who spends a fortune on hemp clothing. 


Option B: Property Developer who is another Quiet Achiever. No one knows how much money he has, where he spends his nights or what his deeper desires are. Some potential advise Eyre: don't believe all the hype about buying a house or houses. I mean, that's fine and dandy if you want to spend all your time accruing wealth, but flat, calm, safe and satisfying ground can be found anywhere your heart is having its desires met. Indeed, chaos is good for the soul.
Nice guy, but a little lost in the adult world most of the time.

Ezekiel is the name of a B-52 nuclear bomber in the US air force. And that’s great. Except one day he’s on a training mission with real nukes on board, and that’s okay too, until a computer malfunction instructs his crew to divert him to Moscow and drop their payload. Poor Ezekiel. It’s not even his fault, really. All incoming radio contact is immediately scrambled, however, and if we don’t stop him, the retaliatory strikes from Russia effectively mean we’re all fucked. 
The moral to the story? Can someone just keep an eye on this young man for us, from time to time?….thanks.

His hair is curly because he is sufficiently electrifying, hence I would advise not getting too close to him if there’s a lightning storm overhead, and you are either wet or standing on some kind of metal. He’s a great fire twirler.
See Fabio, except you’d be wrong to think Fab isn’t an intelligent or thoughtful individual. And he’s more creative than he lets on.
A flittering-nothing-fable of a character, who kind of wanders around aimlessly like a ghost with current-existence issues.
Fabulous Fabio is a big guy with an Italian heritage and a big ego. He works out at the gym and he's proud of the result. And...ahh...yep.....he's proud of the result. (Do anything for you, though.)

For such an 'out there', extravagant, Italian-Stallion kind of name, Fabrizio is remarkably calm and gentle. Like a wild horse that has been broken-in to the tune of 79%, only rarely does he threaten anyone, and if he does it's for a bloody good reason. True to form, only those who meet him behind closed doors will see the full swell of passion the man possesses. Great with kids, although he makes a more playful uncle than father.

Well, I guess we should be thankful his parents never called him Tea Strainer. Falk likes things to be done well and he likes it when people put in a good effort. It doesn't matter if things go to shit and you make a hell of a mess, so long as  you attempt to do whatever it is you're doing, well, then he'll give  you your due. Things can change quickly, Falk is all too well-aware of this, and so all he wants is for the best in this moment with the knowledge we have.
Is he a lawyer? He probably should have been because he is a cocky shit. Rude to waiters.
Farren applies himself well and without the need for adulation….well, almost. His failures effect him deeply and he is a man of his word. He might even be a little bit shy.
Eat a dick.

A rather replete individual who knows who he is, knows what he enjoys and makes no bones about the fact that his chubby cheeks are part of the deal. If he's lean of stature then Fatman is an uncompromising negotiator who won't take no for an answer.

The gifted madman. His artistic talents are weighed up against a set of deluded self-beliefs which include buying in to every conspiracy theory he comes across. At night he stares at the youtube for hours, until finally writing down all his spells and casting the pieces of paper into a cauldron, in the hope of single-handedly achieving the collapse of western civilisation. Beware!
Fazio is a social butterfly that sticks to the pubs, clubs and cafes near the beach. He is a shit hot dancer and carries a permanent erection.

Funny little fucker, isn’t he? He has an answer for everything, a joke for everyone and penny for the homeless. He just needs a good wash once in a while if he’s going to have any chance with the ladies.
The loveable bank robber.
Like a non-violent one-man A-team, if you need something fixed, get Fence. The End.
A cross between a still Irish glen, an ancient Otway fern and a Tasmanian pig pen at feeding time, Fenn is both tranquil and ridiculous.
His IQ score is in the top 0.5% of the population, which explains why he’s so fast with the perfect one-liner. Apart from being very funny, Fergus is one of the true sexual deviants.

Sure, he's woken up on a strange floor a few times but he goes hard at the partying caper like he goes hard everywhere. He learns fast and is always busy, which is why Ferris succeeds at most things in life. As a definite ‘pants man’ he’s hard to pin down for a long-term loving commitment, but he’ll try anything once.
A doer and provider of services and goods.
Come on - do some work you lazy shit!

The lone policeman in a small country town. Everyone knows his name and nearly everyone respects him as a decent bloke who is doing a good job by doing the best he can, while at the same time always giving people the benefit of the doubt.

Sure, he loves his Guiness but most of all he loves a small but loud gathering where music and laughter echo through to outside. He isn't the only person in the Kingdom to feel this way but he's one of the few that endeavours to cultivate such a setting as a regular hobby. Finian.

Rarely deprived of the finer things, let alone a decent family upbringing, Finlay forges through life like a person swimming the breast-stroke, and who performs it quite well. Trouble is, if there is a rip or a shark nearby and he needs to swim quickly, his freestyle stroke is bloody awful which means he cant get anywhere in a hurry. Indeed, if he sticks his head in the water for too long he'll drown. But, so long as he keeps his chin above the surface and carefully watches the currents around him, and the shore, he'll do well. Finlay.

Yes, you guessed it, as a member of the Oxford 8, Finley has attitude and his parents probably have some cash, which can be nice. But disregarding that, Finley's role in the boat is one of comic relief. Sure, he aches and agonises just as much as anyone, but what's the point fucking complaining. Someone has to keep the spirits up, old boy, and here is the man for the job. Indeed, he doesn't take too much seriously, which, like most things, can be a blessing and a curse.

Having arrived at the last of his reincarnations, Finn is not far from the finish line and it makes sense then that he is a placid and ostensibly good individual. None of us are going to feel like having a full-on party at the end, anyway.
Finnegan wears a Devil's pentogram around his neck.

Finnegan may have a strange amulet around his neck, sure, but he certainly has a pudgy, nuggety little fishing boat. He catches very few fish and seems to spend most of his time painting it and sharing a smoke and a joke with some of the other fishermen in the boat yard who, like him, should try spending more time fishing and less time gas-bagging.
A calm individual who incapable of rushing. He is therefore a meticulous plate drier.
The trout fisherman who is both patient and peculiar.

What a rather lovely and singular man. Fionn (pronounced Finn )operates from a very centred space most of the time and while he's not hyperactive, thank god, boys will be boys. His friends, like him, are interesting and considerate, and with regards to romance he enjoys spending a long time with one person, rather than leaving a trail of pining short-term hearts. As for a career, all we can say is that he has an artistic edge. He's no motor mechanic.

Completely unrelated to his female counterpart, Fish is extremely lucky and he’s English. He drinks hard, he plays harder and after he left the army he wound up working for a Sheik in Saudi Arabia. No one knows what he does, and he’d be hard pressed to explain it himself.

Yeah, well, no surprises here kids. Fisk is a canny operator who has never been bored in his life. He sees through useless/un-giving people in an instant and they can expect never to encounter him again. He doesn't mind hard physical work but there must be a larger plan in the offing, and one that involves mental stimulation. As soon as his thinking brain is disengaged then the game is up. And, if he is (very occasionally) rude and/or manipulative it's only because he has grasped the situation before those around him. He's rarely broke, although he's very happy to declare bankruptcy over and over again if he needs to.
Redneck.
Loves reading highly detailed maps.
Not as ballsy as you might think, Flashy is actually a picture of conservatism around the house and home. He plans well in business and he’s never deliberately ripped anyone off.

Well, you can't deny his enthusiasm, can you. Batman, Ironman, Thor, The Green Lantern and, of course, the one he plans to pull out on his wedding night, Superman, are just some of the costumes he likes to bring into the bedroom for play behind closed doors. To be honest, they're the main reason that many of his girlfriends decided to stay with him for as long as they did.

Is Fleetwood a simpleton?
No.
Is he lazy?
He used to be.
Is he a musician?
Thankfully, no.
Does he work hard?
He’s matured with age, let’s just say that.
Is he tired of the references to the band?
Of course.
In summation, Fleetwood is over the hustle and the bustle of modern, city living. He wants to live the quiet life, maybe on some property with a good garden and a few animals to entertain his kids. This would be enough for Fleetwood.

Fletch is so laid back that he hardly gets anything done. He is, however, arguably the calmest person in the Kingdom in that he never panics, ever, and the last breath of air that he takes before leaving this life will be used to tell some kind of joke.
Fletcher cuddles like a big furry Kodiak Bear.
The disappearing act. We’re sure he’s good fun but no one ever seems to know where he is.

Well-dressed in natural fibres, Florian has good hair and attracts the ladies. Question is, are they powerful, ridiculous, funny and memorable ladies? Either way, Florian hangs out near the art scene and various auction houses where he is always on the lookout for a bargain.
The buffoon with good looks – albeit, a buffoon with a rousing sense of humour because, not only does he know he’s a buffoon, he actually goes out of his way to tell others he’s a buffoon.
Girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls, girls (unless he's other way inclined), then sleep.

Fog is the sort of fellow who will take up a position as director of a scientific research station on a small tropical island. Not one to sit idle, Fog will use his post to (A) meet and bed as many female researchers as he can and (B) grow and sell crops of marijuana.
Don't give him blackness. Give him lights. Big, shiny disco lights with plenty of loud music and pretty girls. He ain't no mover and shaker but he's certainly a player.

In his own mind, his life peaked when he had his own roped-off section inside the VIP area, in one of London's classier second tier nightclubs. Anything else, Fox, or is that the sum of of your greatest achievements?...

At some point in his life Foxy will exactly resemble the four-legged variety and much of that guile has carried over because he is a wonderful and enigmatic smart arse, who’ll only end up in the rubbish if his girlfriend kicks him out of the house for being drunk.

Always looking for shortcuts, Foz grew pot under his house for years until the cops came round in an unrelated matter. Foz was so used to his lifestyle by then he didn't think twice about answering the door with a joint in his hand. The rest is history. Now he's a priest.
Naughty, not silly and more than just a tiny bit perverted, Francesco was once kicked out of high school for boring a hole through the wall of the girls' change rooms.

The Sicilian tomato farmer who migrated in the 60's and grew lots of white chest hair. His original name was Luigi but he changed it after he arrived so he would fit in, and he has one of the strongest handshake grips in the world. Don't even think about looking at his daughter.
One of the world’s generous men. Regardless of that, Frank can speak for quite a while without actually saying very much.

Frankie is the name of the fellow who sells hotdogs out the front of the disco after it shuts. He loves pretty young girls and he loves hotdogs with onion, mustard and lots of tomato sauce, but get him drunk and you might see a different fellow, altogether – possibly a dangerous and crazy one.
Franklin drifts off to sleep at night dreaming about the number of properties he’ll one day own.
The Lighthouse.
Franz will prod and poke and nudge and bump you, until he's got you figured out.
Whether he has a chip on his shoulder or not, Fraser has huge reserves of energy that compel him to live a busy life. And he’ll never back down from a fight, even if he is bleeding badly.
Sociopath. A nice one, though. He won't bite.

Metaphorically, Fred is like a 1200 year old Huon pine resting undisturbed in a secluded section of the western Tasmanian wilderness. Some woodchoppers saw him once, years ago, and elected to leave him be and to this day he casts a loving eye over his beloved forest. He has survived generations of howling gales from the roaring forties and he never gets tired of celebrating his life by closing his eyes and swaying in a warm afternoon breeze. And what does all this mean for our young Fred? In human terms he is perpetually young, perpetually optimistic and he never gets too caught up in either the future or the past. Life is here, so why not be a little silly and try to live peacefully and happily in this moment. Thanks Fred.
The name of the bloke that runs the meat tray raffle at the footy club every Saturday night.

Frederick is a Swedish backpacker living some-where between Bondi Beach and Port Douglas, or the Greek islands or the California coast. He is just over 6 feet tall, has blonde eyebrows and is kind of skinny.
Well I suppose he is, but I wonder if his staff feel the same way? Are they paid enough, sir? So come on, don’t be a tight arse. Management.
A clean and methodical man whose pet is a rather temperamental Great Dane.
Frog is another all-round nice guy, and the most we can say about his capacity to save world is that he is here.
Fudgie has a super quick wit, but because the world expects him to come in second, or a second later than he could, he does. And so, bugger that idea Fudgie. Do it your way.
I know, just relax. The crew up here in the box think you should head on over to Finn. Cheers.
One of the happy guys. G lends a hand, he smiles and he laughs more than most, and all this macho crap too many men seem to put on is basically none of his business. But, he's no sissy.
An energetic, kind and busy young man who darts about the world with a strange kind of athletic elegance.
A serious fellow with brooding looks and dark hair.
Well-travelled, artistic, educated and competitive – be it in the kitchen or as a downhill skier – Gæton tends to live large.

City dweller. He knows most of the shortcuts around town, his first reaction is to look serious rather than to smile (which, for some reason unbeknown to us, many girls find quite attractive) and he takes a while to let his guard down. He always gives the impression he’s about to leave.
Yes, one r, two r's, it doesn't really matter G. Check out Garreth. You two are cut from the same chunk of whatever it is you're made from. (We're still waiting for the geology reports to come back.)

Yes, he exists in the flesh. At work he’s surprisingly attentive and competent, but out here in civilian-land he’s a funny ratbag, as you’d expect. Old ladies just want to cuddle him up and stick him in their handbag.
Calm. At peace. Garret is the kind of man who, as a lone father, would have no reservations at taking his two young children on a three month tour of India.
Garreth is purposeful with a giant intellect. Yes, the undertow of a hidden ego lurks here but make no mistake, Garreth is capable of absolute greatness…not that you’re ever likely to hear about it.
A likely lad who believes life is short.

It is of some small surprise for those who meet Garrie that he is not as laconic as his close cousins (below) and definitely more educated. Not pigeon-holed into a life of manual labour, Garrie has artistic edges which means anything is possible, although he is reasonably tired of having to correct the spelling of his name.

(Yeah, I know - there are two R's in your name but suck it up sunshine.) There’s a red wine stain on the lounge room carpet that you/he left one night after he/you turned up drunk and unannounced. Moral to the story: if you've had a few and you get a rush of blood for a visit, do us a favour and just give us a ring beforehand, eh? Thanks. Management.
As a pick-up line to a girl, he’ll say, “......umm...do you wanna’ go outside....and umm....check out your pool?” By the end of saying it even he is visibly wincing at how pathetic it sounds.
There’s a red wine stain on the lounge room carpet that he left one night after he turned up drunk and unannounced.

Gator doesn’t live in Zurich or Chicago or Stockholm because he’s better suited to a much warmer clime. This doesn’t stop him from planning well, however, and he therefore tends to do things properly, wasting no or little energy in the process.

Whether he’s a large dopey bloke from Miami, who watches a heap of TV and puts away at least half a case of beer each night, an eccentric gay hairdresser from Tasmania, who is as fun and famous as he is dangerous, or a mild-mannered engineer from Helsinki, who somehow ended up running the company, Gav is a cool cat who is loved and appreciated by literally everyone.
Elemental. Gavin is genuine and ostensibly tranquil.

Gayne isn't the sort of personality to be affected by pressure or stress. Yes he has his moments, but by and large he is able to see his way around tight moments and corners, rarely getting flustered. He is no fun for his kids to argue with because he barely raises his voice, and therefore never shows signs that their actions are bothersome.

Another who needs no introduction. Gazza is friendly to strangers and forgetful when it comes to things that aren’t in front of his face. As a physical fellow who prefers to use his hands, Gazza enjoys the satisfaction of physically watching a project have a start, a middle and an end. Facebook is rarely any of his business. Gazza is a champ, make no mistake.
Ged is indestructible, paradoxical, sarcastic and sufficiently enigmatic.
Ever seen the group-orgy scene in the movie, ‘Eyes Wide Shut’? Well, in the real world, Geeves organises these things for a living.

The captain of the team, the founder of the company and a leader when a vaccum appears. Will he break the rules? If he thinks they are not worthy, sure. Indeed, his arrogance is something to be lauded not feared. Someone has to trailblaze. (Don't forget, however, that Gene can be a big softie as well.)
The Evil Uncle.

Regardless if he owns a construction company or is involved in the conservation movement, this fellow is basically rock-solid with the odd sprinkle of greatness at the edges. (He is unique in the car world for his renowned reliability.)

Georgie is one of those Navy Captains who is liked by his crew. He's good at his job, which is one thing, and he has a rather laid-back demeanour, which they appreciate because it means they can talk to him, but he commands respect because when the shit hits the fan his orders are clear and consice, his course of action is generally correct and, touch wood, they know he'd be the one to go down with the ship if he had to.
Plonk goes the dollop of cream on top of the apple pie.
Never without a multitude of friends, Georgie is a big kid at heart who, at the tender age of 55, is liable to have a very young wife.
A lovely old fellow that lives on his own and plays the piano in the nude.

As a young man he was once kicked out of a nightclub for trying to sneak into the girl’s toilet and watch one of them take a pee, but not long after that he discovered God and became determined to cleanse himself of such damnations. Today, as a man of the cloth, he often wears a funny white gown and speaks in dramatic tones with his hands held in the air, in the same way that a doctor walks into an operating theatre having just washed them. Very odd.

Gerhard rarely attends the circus because he resents the clowns. How can a person get through life devoid of serious responsibilities? This is the question he would ask them if ever he was introduced. He likes the animals though, the bigger the better. The elephants especially, mainly because he sees himself reflected in their personalities. In his eyes they seem like patient and very intelligent creatures, not prone to fits of panic or illusion. If only he knew the truth!

Very spelling-aware in lieu of the continual misspellings of his name, which in turn has made him quite careful in life, Gerrie's height gives him a certain presence and his children are generally well-educated. 
Question: Is Gerrie similar to David Lee Roth? (Ex-lead singer of a band called Van Halen. Google him if you’ve never heard of him)
Anyway…

Answer: No.

A very patient home builder/renovator. Yes, the plans look great, the weather seems to be fine for the next few months and money isn't an issue, but unforeseen mishaps are a CERTAINTY. Gerrit is very aware of this, which is why, no matter what happens, he's always watchful about how things are progressing. He never ever gets ahead of himself, even in the bedroom, which some might consider a pity.

Gerry is not as outlandish as one might think. He walks with an easy gait and he has the capacity to marvel at the tiny things as well as the large. At his core he is a calm and searching soul who listens and observes, offering advice only when asked or if a situation or person obviously requires it.

I don't know he does it, really, but Gery's life seems to be remarkably devoid of boring rigmarole. Maybe it's that hard 'g' at the start of his name that sets him off in a direction quickly and without hesitation, and let's face it, hesitation is the harbinger of red-tape and useless caffuffle. Know what I mean?

(Good mates with Dick.)
Giaan is deep. He designs sunglasses. He even sleeps with them on.

Giacomo stands on the deck of his Spanish Galleon with a wench in one hand and a telescope in the other, searching the horizon for any generally irresponsible mischief to be had. (Like Nick a little later on, he’s barely heard of the Tax Office.)
The passionate and gentle Italian man, whether he’s Italian or not. His parents might just love Italy, which happens sometimes.
Enthusiastic. Doesn’t sleep much.

Smooth. Gib doesn’t mess around with useless deeds or thoughts and he only falls to pieces if kept inside for too long where there is a good chance he will suddenly turn into some kind of caged animal. He’d die if he had to spend a winter in Sweden, although, having said that, he’d probably satiate his sense of adventure by stealing away with a pack of huskies and a dog sled where he’d quite happily feast on raw venison until he got bored with the lack of girls to chase – or be chased by.

Option A: A big, beer drinking, chauvinistic Queenslander/Texan.

Option B: The name of a colourful old blanket that is tossed over the back of a donkey in a Spaghetti Western. As such, he’s an ideal contact if you intend to carry guns, drugs or tequila.

No, he's no flower posy. He's more like the shovel in the hands of a gardener who knows how to wield one. Gibbs shares a joke and he's a laid-back character, but when he gets down to work - and it can't be too technical or complex - he puts his head down and tries as best he can. Drinks too much.
Musician, artist, hippy, philosopher, grave digger or glass blower: this is where you will find him.
Gidz is a cynical, if not a very humorous individual. If watching an ad on TV that he detests, he will leap to his feet and swear that he’ll never buy that product again. And he never will.

Gil inhabits one of those bodies in which is it nigh' impossible to ascertain what he does for a living. For instance, he might be so funny and gregarious that you would presume he's a stand-up comedian when in fact he is a civil engineer. Or maybe he's a plumber in his day job, with mud and dirt perpetually underneath his fingernails, who has a world famous butterfly collection? Perhaps he's a mild-mannered dog breeder who is awkward in large groups of humans, and who on the weekend turns into an avid skydiver? I suppose Gil never feels the need to boast, we're not sure, but he's certainly worth following.

Has any one person gotten away with more? Sure, someone like Alby might but he's quite open about his irresponsibilites. Gilbert on the other hand slips around situations like an unseen snake, whisking away money, goods and womens' hearts like its nobodies business. How do you do that Gilbert?

Defence attache, is his job title. We can't tell you what he really does - it's top secret - and you'd never consider him someone who would do such a job, only because the car he drives, the women he hangs out with and number of famous people in his phone are more akin to a Hollywood A-lister.
Has he been shot at? Yes.
He can't remember the last time he was bored.

"I say, George, do you mind dropping the Maserati off for a service this week? And if you don't mind, I think it's time to dust off the 'roller. Do you mind doing that for this afternoon?.....Splendid."
What is it with Frenchmen? They talk loudly, frown heavily at things that are inconsequential to most people and this one - well, to say he has a wandering eye would be an understatement.

As a Japanese girl in past life he has a fetish for Asian Kung-Fu movies. Gilly rhymes with ‘Hii-yaaaa!!!’, after all. And he’s one of the few people on earth whose smile is actually wider than their face, which aids him to be one of the world’s truly generous men.

The Gimp loves burrowing down inside his hole and meditating. In a good mood he ponders things like love and the synchronicity of the universe. In a bad one he licks his lips and conjures up notions of perfect evil.

Gino is the only man to work at the tax department who has been investigated by the tax department. On his gravestone will be the following epitaph:

Keep your friends close and your enemies closer.

How can one person lie so much and yet be loved as much as they are? We're still trying to come to terms with that one. Just don't make him the captain of any large ship because it'll all end in tears. Trust me.
A preposterous galoot.

Glen is like the state of California in that he is affluent, good company (generally) and occasionally ‘out there’, but through the middle of him runs something akin to the San Andreas fault. The question is, when and/or will the entire state suddenly tear apart and slip into the Pacific Ocean? Who knows.....maybe it won’t?

Glenn is like the state of California in that he is affluent, good company (generally) and occasionally ‘out there’, but through the middle of him runs something akin to the San Andreas fault. The question is, when and/or will the entire state suddenly tear apart and slip into the Pacific Ocean? Who knows.....maybe it won’t? (And yes, that's right, the double N doesn't change a thing, apart from highlighting the fact that at least one of parents is completely fucking dyslexic.)
Nice guy. He's a snob, sure, but he's okay.

Similar to a very large and expensive ocean liner which has lost the use of its rudder, Glenville moves reasonably slowly. A fine looking vessel however, and we expect the salvagers will make a killing. (ie: Glenville may very well inherit a bucket of money, but unlike the previous generation who earned it, he will do a fine job of wasting the lot.)
The Gifted Cartoonist.
Twinkle Toes. A delightful fellow.

Googie is a light-hearted soul who doesn’t actively decide anything at all. Years ago he read a book called The Dice Man and in allowing ‘the universe’ to dictate how his life unfolds, it has never been the same since. God only knows what he’s up to today...

A large, bustling man who does very little in a meek fashion. He’s up for a hair-brain scheme, he’s up for a bit of hanky panky, and he’ll try anything once. 95% of Gordos have a kind heart, so none of his carry on carries any malice, praise be the lord.
Gordon is a big personality and a great hulk of a man in body and/or spirit. He’s rollicking fun at dinner parties, for instance, until he gets pissed and tries to lift up all the girls’ skirts.

A fierce competitor who is outraged by acts of prejudice against the innocent. Sure, his sense of humour might need some work, but it's not his fault. In a past life he was once slayed on a Scottish moor defending his clan and so how do you reckon he was going to turn out?

Goughie rhymes with, ‘Jesus, that was close..’, as well as, ‘Anyone seen the remote?’
Overall, Goughie gets on with life in a no-nonsense fashion, cruising with the luck that he seems to generate himself. His approach has paid off because the result is a contented bloke who is more than happy to put on his girlfriends’ bathers at a moment’s notice.

Born on the land, Goulbourne knows a lot more about soil, crops, wethers and motors than the latest theories on the whereabouts of the G-spot. Indeed, Goulbourne, mate, do you even know what a clitoris does?…..We’ll leave it with you. Good luck.

Like a big and somewhat dopey Red Setter, Goz has more friends than he knows what to do with. His girlfriends/partners need to be funny as well, and if they can hold their liquor then all the better. Goz is easily pleased but laughter in his life is a must. His needs are relatively simple and he is good with his hands, so if you have one we suggest you take him out in the countryside and let him run free for a while…maybe throw him a big juicy bone when he’s finished.
Probably too intelligent for his own good. Graco is extremely charismatic and he does play games, although he only does it to give himself something to do because most people bore him, shitless.

Like his female counterpart, Grady seems to appear from out of nowhere. He's nowhere near as compassionate as her though. We suspect he's a vampire, which would explain things. True, he's not the only vampire out there, but he's safe enough.
Graeme is like water. In the driest continent on Earth, therefore, he is an iconic figure because he provides energy and life without any fanfare. I’m not sure where any of us would be without him.
Graham is basically the same as his brother (Graeme) but he isn’t as good at getting his hands dirty.
Grant is potent and single-minded. He’s often misread as a bully or a grouch but that’s not right – he’s just doing what it takes.
An eccentric Scottish Lord who either drinks whisky while playing golf, or drinks whisky while shooting peasants…..oops...I mean, pheasants.
Gratias is as quiet as a mouse until he gets pissed with the boys.

Option A: Plain like a pancake without anything on it. Greg is so plain, in fact, he is occasionally a little perplexed by his own boring normalness. But don’t think for a second that if push comes to shove he can’t (and won’t) stand up for what he believes in. (In a past life he was a pilot of an RAF Lancaster bomber which was shot up and in flames over Germany, and he refused to bail-out until each of his surviving crew members had made it out first…)

Option B: The current president of the National Association for Nudists, which proves Greg is rarely as dull as you might imagine.

Ever seen the first Independence Day movie? Anyway, Gregg is just like the maths professor who saves the world. He watches all the fools squawk and yell and carry on, clambering for either attention, love or money, until he thinks everyone is ready to hear what he has secretly discovered. Usually, no one else has thought of it. That aside, throughout nearly all aspects of his life Gregg retains a splendid, happy demeanour, he's rarely rushed and he's always on the lookout for anything weird or kinky. You can give him shit about his name if you like, but he'd just think of you in the same way we would - you're probably a buffoon and therefore worthy of being either ignored or pitied. Have a nice day.

Never judge a book by its cover. An intellect of gargantuan proportions lies undiscovered here, so what if he has Asperger's Syndrome? Society and its rules are usually full of crap anyway. Remember this: Gregor is here to help and here to help others laugh as well, no matter what his profession.
Gregory died out in the early 80’s when the ozone layer started to disappear. It was probably a blessing.
The aloof stalker who keeps a stash of Rohipnol in his cupboard.

House painter. Funny as a whip. At the end of the day you can see him out the back of the house laughing with his crew. They're all covered in paint and they all smoke - as if the paint fumes aren't harmful enough - but that's okay. The day is over and they all aim to be better men next week. Whose shout is it anyway?

Griffin seems to deal with life as if he is a Sultan Prince who has been magically tranported into the body of a young western middle class man, who needs a job but hasn't got one, and who really doesn't want one.
Grof is like one of those big poodles that, when he looks at  you, you'd swear is actually a small man in a very hairy jacket. Funny guy. Loves a cuddle.

Well, yes, he’ll get his hands dirty, but you’d be hard pressed to find a person who works harder. He thinks on his feet, has excellent common sense, can read people like a book almost on first sight and is incredibly loyal. In a past life he was head engineer/armorer for a bomber squadron in England, during World War 2, and his heart broke every time one of his planes didn't made it back.
Guido is one twisted mother fucker, be it sexually or otherwise.
A dreamer. We suspect he'd like to be a realist but we're glad he's not. Guiseppe.
Yeah, but can he play? Or is he so sick of the expectation that he never wants to look at a guitar ever again?...
The cocky loud-mouth.
A good team man in any sports club.

Possibly Dutch, Gunter is a marvellous specimen. He approaches every moment with fresh eyes and ears, and his dogged optimism would be worth millions if one could only bottle it. And he has a genuine, welcoming laugh.
No hidden tricks here, folks. Guppy plays pretty hard, he begrudgingly works pretty hard, and all in all he’s worth his due.

Gus was a roo shooter for years until he discovered how much he enjoyed being at sea, and where he truly discovered the effects of gravity and momentum. The last I heard he was driving fishing boats in either the Southern Ocean or the Irish Sea, but he's always been good with engines.
He looks and sounds gruff but trust me, Gustav is just a big, playful teddy bear.

17 years old no matter how old he is, Guy has a terrible time trying to explain why and how a 41 year old man has as many wet dreams as he does. In life, his decisions are often rash and he’s a hopeless lover, but it’s not all bad because he’s one of the few men that has the capacity to autofellate. Disregarding his sexual prowess, Guy is a wonderful harbinger of change and therefore one of the most optimistic people in the room.

First things first, we need to get a DNA sample from him just to confirm our theory, but he’s no fool. If Gyrin suspects we’re onto him he’ll be off like a shot, and it’s not as if he doesn’t know how to blend into the background. He also knows how to break the rules, as most alien creatures here on Earth are prone to do. But you won’t find Gyrin conducting his human-observational studies way out in the middle of nowhere. Shit no. You’ll find him up to his neck in some kind of absurd social life where the spotlight isn’t far off, and where he’s managed to convince everyone he’s a brilliant human artist/raconteur. Funny thing is, he actually is, and he doesn’t mind you knowing about it either, bless his alien cotton socks. Amen.
Lonestar.

Easy going? Suuuuuuure, he is! Seemingly fun and irreverent on the surface, Hadassah is incredibly competitive. Is he narrow-minded? Well, we hope not. If he's born in the Middle East he might need to take a chill-pill once in a while, but generally he's okay. (Good friends with Aaron.)

By the time people figure out how his name is spelled Hadrian has come right around and sorted out his shit. So, in life, Hadrian will stick to the programme for longer than you think and almost certainly for longer than you'd hope. No, he's not a boring bastard, but he won't leap of cliff in the nude, first. Girls meet him and presume he is either important or cashed up, and we can tell you he has that potential, if that's your thing, but we suggest he lives with his shoes off for as long as he can. It'll do him good.
The absurd and hilarious Scotsman who, while a long way from home, is at home everywhere he goes.
Haim in never home which worries his parents constantly, although they are well aware that his life decisions are reasonable and well thought out.

Hal rhymes with Have As Much Fun As Is Reasonably Possible, it rhymes with Think About What You Want and it rhymes with Understand The Consequences Of Your Actions. In short, Hal is a wonderful old sage whose presence opens people up.

Hallam is tired of being called Helen, which happens if he stays at the pub late on a Friday night. At least, it used to happen until he decided to stop going. Having said all that, he does like snake skin boots so who knows, maybe there is a hidden Helen in there after all?
A pontificating loon.
A reliable and kind-hearted fellow who doesn’t beat around the bush despite being raised there. “Are you talking to me?” he asks with complete sincerity. “What do you want?”

The name of the filthy fat man who is driving the tow-truck that comes to rescue you in a dodgy part of town at 3 o’clock in the morning. You can smell his body odour before he gets out of the truck, which in itself is also bad for the environment, and he is one of the most splendid visions you have ever seen in your life.

It's 3 o'clock in the morning and the mud-crabbing trip has gotten off to an inauspicious start. For the last two hours we've been progressively bogged five different times in a tropical swamp. No one is in peril as there's plenty of beer - we didn't bring any water with us, fuck that - and the crocs are rarely seen this far inland so nobody is going to get eaten. We hope. Just as it seemed we'd cleared the bad bit, however, we've hit one more swampy patch that has gotten us bogged again. “Fucken hell!” everyone curses, just about fed up. Ahead of the troopy we can see that the ground is higher and drier, we think, and just as with everything in life, it seems, here again is one final hurdle we have to jump over before we hit pay-dirt. At this pivotal moment, covered in mud and cold as buggery, the right blend of 'Hanlon' within the group is critical (i.e: the right blend of nous, determination and humour).
If we've got it, we'll get through, have a laugh, drink some piss, catch some muddies' and have a fat time. If we haven’t got any then we're fucked and we're in for a cunt of a night.

Hanno never dies wondering. And if he fails, well at least he had a go and stuff the consequences! If we could bottle him and feed him to the nation we might bloody-well change the fate of the planet. Who knows? (Yes, he's ungainly on the dance floor but he can handle a rifle.)

Like all northern European men Hans laughs at the weirdest things. Never unfriendly and always extremely well-travelled and intelligent, Hans has come to understand what he wants from life and how he wants to live. Rules have never impacted him and he is an independent thinker. Is he a sexual deviant? Mmm, well, we can't say that he is but, equally, we can say he’s more than comfortable being nude in a public place.

Hardie drives a Range Rover and he isn't one of these people who never uses its off-road capacity. He enjoys quality in both the people that he mingles with and what he surrounds himself with in life. Well-travelled and well-fed, when he gets there, Hardie will be a cheerful old man who looks a lot more serious than he is. He smokes a pipe and he gets in trouble for flirting with the nurses.

Hardy never seeks the spotlight. He’s far more concerned with doing the right thing by the planet, by his kids and by the community at large. As a young man he was damn-near reckless in his various pursuits.

Haren is a wonderful and quirky little fellow who fossicks about with some kind of constant smile on his face, like he is about to engage in something so ridiculously fun and childishly stupid that he can barely contain himself.

Hari's house is like a little slice of India. It's full of incence smoke, strange Hindi hangings on the wall, loud twanging Indian music and, while I'm not certain of course, I think that basket in the corner contains a living cobra.
Succinct in dealings and emotionless to those who don’t know him, Haris exists as a reminder that nothing in life is straightforward.

Now here is an understated, cool cat. No, Harl isn't shy, he just likes to sit back for a while and take it all in, analyse what's going on around him, let the cafuffle die down before he speaks his piece or makes his move. If you tell Harl a joke and you've just met him, he'll look you in the eye and listen to what you're saying, but all the while at the back of his mind he is endeavouring to look into your soul so see who you really are. To be honest, it's quite a gift. He's no street-sweeper.
Outlandish? Nay. Friendly? Yay. Boring? Nay. Lonely? Fucking never.
Harley is light on his feet and he’d make an excellent thief, rapper or kick-boxer.
Harold wears full pyjamas to bed every night and tries to sit very straight whenever he eats. It’s good for the digestive system.
Another chest waxer. (his)
