Like Stretch after him, his physique is assumed except that he is oh-so sensitive. Skinny is on life number 2 and he knows it but, like Rhonda way before him, he’s searching desperately for the answers (which probably means that he’s actually on life number 5).
A nice guy and perhaps a little too nice. Skip is pretty gullable and, like Cecily way before him, he gives more than he recieves. Give him a job where he's occupied and he'll be happy for hours.
Like his female namesake, the universe presents him with a giant blank canvas. No violent streaks here folks. Skye is a lovely, gentle man.
Doink.

Hmmm....is he slippery like Simon? Is he shifty like Solomon? We don't think so, he's not that bright. But, he does tend to make the most of his opportunities, which is fine, so long as his actions and words arise from a position of compassion and forgiveness. Is that the story Slater?...

You can imagine the hive of activity in one of London’s best restaurants knowing Prince Harry is dining this evening. Slav, the head chef, agrees to show Harry around the kitchen afterwards but just as Harry enters the space, Slav is caught off guard by an ill-placed tomato broth and an unseen puddle of water on the floor. Harry walks though the doors just as Slav slips over in the kitchen for the first time in 15 years, and hits the deck in unison with 5 litres of puree which spills all over him. 
“So, how was dinner, Harry?” Slav asks, looking up and wiping the broth out of his eyes.
Harry smiles. “Splendid Slav, just splendid. I just wanted to say how much I enjoyed dinner. Lucky I didn’t order the tomato soup, eh?”
“Yes, well, I can tell you that it tastes great.”
“Mmmm, it looks it.”


This is classic Slav.
True to the cause. He can pick a faker a long way off.

If Smiddy is a room full of people then there is only one of them on Earth. I have no idea what would happen to the universe if ever there were two. It might just implode for something funny and cool to do. Who knows....

Whether he’s about to speak with the Prime Minister or he’s in the middle of getting 4 crazy kids off to school, it’s difficult for Smiley to get loaded up with the stresses of responsibility. His name catches the world off-guard, which keeps him light on his feet, partially because he is continually on the look-out for anything new; be it weird coincidences, new toys, unusual recipes or undiscovered coral species. 
(Closet sexual deviant.)

Ooookay, so either mum was besotted with the waiter-character from the TV show, Sex In The City, or….hang on…in fact….there is no ‘either’. 
Smith’s mother was infatuated with the Smith waiter-character from the TV show Sex In The City, and there it is. But what does this mean? Oddly enough, Smith does alright. He’s understated, although, yes, his ego isn’t minimal, but he’s in for good people and good times, and he’ll assist strangers if he remembers that he can. He’s not a total dill, by a long shot.

You say his name, and it sweeps over the ground barely touching it. What does that mean, you ask? Well, it means that he's rarely in one spot for very long, he picks up friends easily - sometimes too easily, so his girlfriends will tell you! - he lives in the moment and he doesn't really like clutter. Smithy.
Pass. Is he a drug dealer?..Anyone?

His friends are all men aside from his girlfriend, who tolerates his excessive drinking. Usually she’s partaking and in that regard they’re a good couple. Snapper spends a lot of time talking about engines and possibly boats. Never done so much as a sit-up in his life.

You’ve entered the lift and next stop, Bang, the head of the company steps in. And you’ve always had an idea, haven’t you? You now have 30 seconds to pitch it to them from a random, standing start, and if it’s good they’ll listen:
Sol lives for these moments. It’s why he’s successful, this coolness under pressure. It makes him think faster and more clearly.
Soon enough,  usually, Sol becomes the boss stepping into the lift, and so life goes around again.

Oh for Christ's sake.....Solaris? (Sigh).......Okay, well let's just ignore mum and dad, who were hoping to produce a unique soul predestined to make a singular, magnificent contribution to human kind. Mmmmm, well, we can tell you Solaris is nice fellow, with a genial approach to life, and a room full of incense sticks, Tibetan prayer flags and books about the Dalai Llama. When he gets back from yoga and brushes the hair out of his face we'll catch up with him and see what he's up to...

The card shark. He speaks in low tones in lieu of all those O’s, which rumble in the back of your throat like the ominous rumblings of an over-regulating government. He understands the tax system backwards.
The Walking Ego, and that's okay. He has a smile on his face and a million friends, most of whom only know him as that big happy guy.
He's a cheeky little bugger, isn't he?

A self-conscious fellow who would do better than he is if he didn't care so much about what others think. Soren, here's a tip, on their death bed everyone is only thinking about what is about to happen next. What you do and how you do it won't get a look in. (We'll talk about your kids another day.)
Your local, friendly drug dealer. Nice guy. But he’s a drug dealer, in case that bothers you.
The remarkable cat with nine lives. (Note: He's got about 2 left....maybe even 1.)
Smooth in water. Ungainly on land.
Spencer loves golf clothes despite his inability to play the game. (He has a fetish for fishnet stockings and he secretly wears them under his trousers during competition.)
Gangly and potentially creepy.
Like his namesake on a mathematical graph, Spike is capable of either the best or the worst and, thankfully, there isn’t too much middle ground.

A man of his word. Yes, he has a sense of humour, but the rigours of a respected male life run deep and are not easily shrugged off. Spiro is therefore rarely flippant and family is very important to him.
Splinter is awkward, hardworking and brave.

Like his namesake from the Starship Enterprise, he was born with gifts that are often misunderstood by those in the human world. The question is, how will he discover them, and what will he do once he does?
The B-grade entrepreneur.

Stacy never sits still for long. He's a quick thinker and a logical one, and he moves over the ground rapidly and with a destination in mind. His family are an odd but lovely bunch and we, up here in the commentary box, believe that most people could actually learn a lot by watching how Stacy performs.
Perpetually surprised and aghast at how poorly his magnificent plan worked out, Stamos refuses to give up. Why would you?
The tall, gentle and unflustered man (on the surface, at least). He’d make an excellent fireman.
Mates with Jim and Bruce, Stan was never the most excitable bloke. He grumbles about the weather.

Stanley tucks his shirt in without fail, he ensures his shoes are nicely polished and when his arthritis allows it, and whenever he’s in such a position, which is a rarity these days, he opens car doors for ladies.
Of Russian extraction, Stas will hold his own, have a laugh with you, but expect that you are able to hold your own, also.

See that horse out there in the equestrian arena prancing around like a bloody trumped-up poodle, with all that ridiculous head-dress regal rubbish all over his face? If Stavros could watch himself fart, he would.

Some of the things St.Clair does to himself in the name of self-pleasuring would make even the most worldly Jake wince. Indeed, they're too graphic even for these pages. So, all we say is, St.Clair, be careful, wash your hands and it's  your turn to cook.

Stede is a city boy and to that end his take on horses is thus: If you can’t put petrol in it don’t get on it. Aside from these urban attitudes, Stede tends to surround himself with the male of the species, which is fine, I suppose. It’s a little boring if you ask us but no one is perfect.
Steele walks around all concerned, as if his nuts are about to drop off. Relax, brother……just relax.

He's not so much a stain on society, as he is a stain on the walls and buildings upon which he applies his not insignificant artistic prowess. 
And we're not talking about just some stock-standard, desperate-looking tag, aching to be recognised. Steen, the boy, and possibly always the boy, has talent, so let's see how he goes...

Stefan rhymes with, “Spitting an olive pip out of your mouth that’s just cut your cheek and nearly cracked a tooth as you bit into it by mistake.” 
(Note: Remembering, of course, that olives are tasty and nutritious, and that Stefan’s substantial physical and/or intellectual capabilities may one day save your life.)

God love him. Yep, his restaurant is going down the drain and he's in debt up to his eyeballs, but you'd never know. The smile and the embrace he gives you as you enter are real, and while behind the curtain things are dire, hospitality is his game and his life. Chin up, Stefano. Things always come good again…

Like a classical pianist, Steinley has clean hands and lean, agile fingers. The neurons in his grey matter are connected up so well and with such intensity that they convey information and imaginings faster than Einstein in his heyday. And best of all, ladies and gentlemen, his eyes sparkle like the Good Witch’s magic crystal ball.......fret not young friar, they cried, for the King is imminent!
See a female Jackie.

Large IQ, low level of patience for fuckwits, high technical ability, no idea how to change the oil in his car, prefers cats to dogs, good under pressure and many people find his sense of humour so dry and pragmatic that they just don't get him.
Cold old axle grease.

Neat, fussy and often lean or small in stature, Stephen won’t wear underpants unless they are properly ironed. By preparing well at every level of his waking life he enables his financial services business to thrive like few others, and he is now quite wealthy as a result. 
(Note: Stephen is completely unrelated to Steve, and he feels very uncomfortable whenever anyone refers to him by that name.)

Steve walks a fine line. V is a powerful letter that can provide immediate greatness, depending on where it is, but if too much time is spent on the ‘ee’ before you get to the V, Steve may well turn out to be a truly sly prick. If it is kept short, however, he can be one of the great individuals. Funny as well. See how you go….
Steven thinks that only immoral women give head.
Stevie is greasy, slimy and sleazy like a low-grade hustler in Mexico City.
Like Walshy and Johnno, everyone knows Stevo’.
An English-styled buffoon who is very polite on the surface.
The hyper-intelligent loner.
Juvenile.

A private school ponce who is the first to volunteer to go into battle for King and country, primarily so he can bed the women who are attracted to his uniform that sports lots of little gold tassels and shiny metal bits from when he once blew up a tribe of African natives using cannons. (He avoids walking near primary schools because all the children point at him and yell, “G’day Peacock!”)

No, he doesn't smile all the time but trust me, it’s a front. Deep down Stoane is a big fuzzy bear just doing his thing, and yes, he can’t move without breaking something but it’s never deliberate. Don’t be frightened.

Does Stone keep his opinions to himself? 
Yes.
Is Stone irresponsible? 
No, he most definitely isn’t, although he’s not always strictly legal. 
Would he forgo the opportunity of stealing a late model BMW convertible sitting unattended by the beach with the keys in the ignition, if he saw a child being swept out to sea? 
Of course he would. Funny thing is, after receiving his bravery award from the mayor at the council chambers, months later, afterwards all he’d have to do is wait around for an hour before he meets with his parole board, which is taking place in the same building.
And don’t you worry, Stone fully appreciates the irony of such situations, which is why we like him.
Stoner is upbeat, energetic and adventurous.

Bloody lost in a storm more like it. Or is that is parents? Anyway, rather than become a tempest, Storm shies away from the spotlight and lets just pray he manages to steer away from the dodgy part of town…
Stretch is a good, humorous and reliable individual who kind of lopes along the street in the same way that he lopes along through life. Like his female namesake, Stretch is invariably tall.

It's the middle of the night and the storm descended on the ketch in a flash. The spinnaker is torn to shreds before anyone can react and suddenly the vessel is in peril. Struan, the first mate, has seen it all before and over the howling noise of the gale he shouts, “Just cut it free. Quickly now.”
The panic-stricken owner begins to protest at a $40,000 sail about to be discarded forever and Struan looks at him calmly. 
“Listen, do you want to live or do you want to die?...”

Soft like a sponge, Stu can deal with any situation. He’s probably the most adaptable and malleable of all the male species and a better absorber of shock or strangeness does not exist. One day he’ll be canonised and we will then know him as St. Stu. And rightly so.

An upstanding member of society who helps out in community projects, such as Meals On Wheels. His mother insists that he eat Sunday lunch at her house every weekend, much to his initial chagrin, although when the apple pie comes out he wouldn’t be anywhere else. And he loves his mum.

Stubbsy collects his beer and his bowl of hot chips from the bar, dodges and weaves back to his friends' table and when he arrives he plonks the beer down, stuffing a couple of chips into his mouth as he sits. Immediately, a horrified look appears on his face. Shocking his friends and all those nearby, Stubbsy pushes his seat back in disgust, stands up again, puts an open palm next to his mouth and yells across a crowded pub, "HEY MATE! YOU FORGOT THE FUCKIN' SALT!"  Stubbsy.
Stuey is a lovely bloke who will do anything for anyone, if need be, (which is a product of the softness of his name) and as a trade-off he often lacks a potent killer-instinct.

Yes, Suede was conceived on the old couch and his parents, bless, wanted to be different. Anyway, Suede is a highly principled lad who will dabble with the arts. Which one, exactly, is uncertain but he definitely won't be doing anything with leather.

What is it with some of you hippies? I'm all for free love in all directions, but honestly! Why didn't you call him Wood-Anchovy? Or Aluminium-Nematode? (Sigh) Anyway, Suede-Butterfly has had earrings since he was 2 months old – like he had a say in the matter – and he’ll go to his grave having not once donned a suit and not once proclaiming to have been in a position of responsibility. So, it’s not all bad.

Deepest darkest Africa. 1930's. Sully blazes into the tent wearing tweed jodpurs and an open white linen shirt, half unbuttoned, covered in sweat and with a rifle slung over his shoulder. He usually exudes charisma and charm, but not today. "There's a flood," he says calmly. "We need to leave. Now." So, with style and not a moment to spare everyone is saved. Sully.

Is Sundeep the most gullible man in the Kingdom? Perhaps. But this generosity of expectation also makes him happy and reasonably loveable. He wants a big family and would probably prefer sons to daughters. (Sundeep, if this is your desire can we suggest that this is unmitigated bullshit and you’ve been brainwashed by your peers and family. Do you think women aren’t at least as powerful as men? They’re definitely more peace-loving.)
Forget corporate achievement or material gain, for Sunny is powered by a different kind of sun – a connected, hilarious and spiritual one.

Like a short lick of a potent and over-ripe cheese, Sven has a unique and complex flavour. He’s a highly intelligent and optimistic fellow and if you’re chasing an intense journey in the name of love or friendship, he could be your man.

Rarely does Swain trod the straight and narrow path. There are always shortcuts, you see. At least in his mind, anyway. There's always an easier route, a smoother passage, a more profitable way of doing things. Swain therefore tends to focus on the desintation not the journey. He'd make a useless Buddhist.

As an outgoing and loudish-mouthed egotist, Swampy is ideal to have around when a group conversation has become uncomfortably stilted. In this setting his presence will be secretly adored by all those present.
Virtuous.

"Ah, well, if it isn't the culprit from last night who stole the car, spilt crap all over the carpet and set fire to the neighbours tree. What are you doing showing your face back here?"
Sylvester kicks the ground in front of him. “Well, I won 30 grand at the casino after I left last night. So I thought I’d come back and mend some bridges.”
Sylvester, mate, we appreciate it, but how about next time we keep the bridges in tact in the first place. Management.

Sylvian is that guy in the movies who is one hurdle away from getting to the treasure. He's crossed the planet, risking life and limb, and you can see in his eyes that he knew he'd get this far. On the other hand, of course, his job is not over and the toughest test is about to begin. Question is, will Sylvian prevail? His French heritage means he loves the constant melodrama, but that’s another story.
Symmo is a blend of Walshy, Johnno, Marty, Dave and Pedro.
Symon has never held a hammer and gets a manicure every fortnight.

"Let me tell you about Taama. He has a largest heart of nearly any man and....WHAT? He's coming around later for a drink?…..Shit, have you got any idea what that means? Alright, don't panic. Here's what we'll do. We'll barricade ourselves inside the front living room, load all our weapons just in case, and try and placate the mad fucker with those steaks in the fridge. After he munches on a couple of those, if we're lucky, he'll just leave and go to the pub. Jesus, last time he was here he tore a hole in the back fence and tried to shag Mrs. Johnson's daughter and I'm not going through that hell again…"

Some people you just like. Even if Tadgh was caught shagging his girlfriend on her mother's couch, one rainy night, by both her parents, somehow their adoration of him would be maintained. Generous smile. Cheeky bastard.

Taggart became an associate at his law firm a week ago, and he was one of the quickest to do so. Aside from the 60+ hours he puts in every week, after work he's parties like a Roman Emperor. How does he do it? Sure, we know he's smart and he's got attitude, but honestly, does he sleep? I suppose Taggart's defining qualities are that (A) he does what he says he's going to do, (B) he loves the macho chest-thumping male competitive life and (C) he’s very aware that he won't be young and vital forever. Taggart.
Taibe isn't the most excitable person in the Kingdom. Hang on, hang on, he's walking but why does he look like he's asleep? Taibe, you awake brother?

Like an introduced species that is actually fun to have around, Tait is an independent cat who does his own thing, and who tends not to destroy either the environment or his fellow animals. Given that he's a carnivore, biologists aren't certain as to how he does this. He might be predominantly nocturnal, which brings with it its own set of problems. Perhaps we need to put a radio tracker on him?

Taite is cool and not the arrogant twat many people perceive him to be. He's actually got a wicked sense of humour, although it took him a while to grow into it. After all, so long as you're not hurting anyone, who cares what anyone thinks of you? Sure, he's a little lazy and he takes ages to hand his assignments in, but he gets them in eventually, which his professors appreciate. And yep, he'll get his degree, at which point he might just as easily disappear into Europe for three years with a backpack strapped to him and disregard his earlier career path completely.
Silky smooth, laid-back and determined, Taj is nowhere near as soft as he sounds. Indeed, he is an incredibly friendly and intuitive soul who has the world at his feet.
The shifty good guy.

The closest thing he’d ever get to a uniform is the soccer jersey for his local club. Talen is a fine and committed (life) player, although he does need a bit of direction. He’d probably make a good soldier, but we suggest he goes out into the world and finds that direction on his own, not via the orders of someone else who is just taking their own orders.
Tallon needs a decent hug. Far more sensitive than he lets on.

Talm is quite combative when he wants to be. Still waters run deeper than you think here and while he's never the loudest of his group, his opinions are respected by those who know him. What does he do for a living? We have no idea but he's not a bean counter.
He's a bizarre cat, alright. Most of the time you won't see him, however, because he'll be digging for old artifacts in Greece, or somewhere.
Up to his eyeballs in debt.
Public speaking isn’t really his thing and he doesn't mind a bit of hard work, once he gets his head around it and gets moving, that is. He's strong and he's loyal, and amen to that brother.

Tamlan likes the idea of strapping on a backpack and disappearing into the wilds of the country side with only a leatherman and a sense of adventure, but if push came to shove, via some cataclysmic event and he actually had to do it, he might struggle. He is a deep thinker however, and rarely does he sit down and say to himself, "You know what, right now I'm content with just about every facet of my life." Keep lookin' lad, keep lookin'.....
Tangi from the Cook Islands. You want, he get.

His reflexes move like a train that has sat on the same piece of line for 30 years and is therefore rusted into place, but he’s an optimistic, funny bloke who can lift a shitload of weight, which has to come in handy sometimes, right?

Raiders of the Lost Ark has a lot to answer for, doesn't it? The city of Tanis, in the movie, is the supposed home of the Ark of the Covenant, which I'm sure is what the parents of Tanis intended him to be. That is, a mystery of god-like proportions that only the very lucky and/or brave will get to behold.
Blah blah blah.....Tanis is a dedicated young man who tends to move with a metal plate stuck to his forehead, which he placed there only to protect his own brain. He tends to run into things head-first, you see, but he’s not a fool. He learned that he had to protect himself. Anyway, that’s Tanis, and this is the life.
A very nice cello.

Now, is that fair? Giving a young man a name that is supposed to turn him into a philosophical juggernaut and worldly sage, in general? But he got over his shyness. He got used to being asked about his name. But he does like spending time on his own, on projects and ideas where he can avoid all those pointless questions and comments from others.

It's not that Tarant is lazy, it's just that he detests all the rigmarole involved with any kind of administration. Sure, many of us can say the same thing, but Tarant will dodge, balk and weave, either literally or metaphorically, so he avoids or delays as much pointless red-tape moments as possible. Does this hold him back sometimes? Well, maybe, but he benefits in other ways by having more free time than most. Which begs the question, what are you doing with your spare time, lad? Are you being good for the world or are you just swanning around in an attempt to stay beneath the radar? (Sometimes the path of least resistance is the longest way round.)

Amen.
A young man brain-washed by images of 6-packed buffoons and absurd hairdos which cover most of your face, Taren needs to toss away his phone and go outside to look at the sky for a while.
"Oh, shit yeah!" he replies, after being asked if he wants to come pig shooting, tonight.
The stealthy crocodile who is either not very bright or just extremely difficult to dissuade from a pre-existing mind-set.

Tarquin is one of those men who, seemingly miraculously, is always, always in tip top form. He is at home inside any social group, his observations are both brilliant and well-timed and he delights in being silly and helping others do the same. There simply isn’t much more to say about the man. Bloody bravo Tarquin.
Rarely a liability, Taryn is open minded and clever.

He's no slacker, but he’s on life number one, according to the reincarnationists, and so his sense of humour, his capacity to be silly and his calm sense of wisdom might take a little longer to evolve.
Ocean kayaker. It's a passtime that provides him with the right blend of sustained physical work, pleasure, fresh air and fresh fish, as well as the odd spot of danger.

Tate loves reconstruction. He might be an air/car crash investigator, a cold case detective or some kind of archeologist. Detail - that's what he's into. And when he gets his teeth into something he's as tenacious as a kelpie.

If you're a lady and you're looking for a fellow who is good with his hands, and who loves a bit of handy work around the house, say, mending the eaves, replacing those old hinges on the bathroom door, or perhaps renovating a bedroom, then Tavis is not your man. The last time he tried to hammer a nail into the wall for that calender he bought (sports cars) he broke his thumb and tore out a huge chunk of plaster which he had to pay to get fixed, and hasn't been game to go near any kind of tool since.

As a ghost that lacks an actual physical body, per se, he gets extremely frustrated, not to mention very thirsty, whenever he attempts to pick up a glass of water because he can’t actually grab the thing. (We hate to say this Tate, but get a job and do it well for 3 months. The stability will do you good.)
See Tay.
He recovered quickly after his sex change operation and now headlines at one of Sydney’s most popular cabaret clubs; big smile, great legs.

Tayne doesn’t really grasp subtle jokes or hidden meanings. If you need to tell him something, don’t paint it up with a flowery metaphor or some kind of smart analogy thinking he’ll get it. He won’t. Just tell him. Likewise, his answers are brief and the only time you’ll hear him speak for long periods is if he has to read a long document, aloud.
The reliable and good-natured show pony.

He’s not a duck! He’s a snake – a great big lazy rainforest python. He drapes himself over limbs all day and likes to chill-out in the shade. He’s a cool customer by default and he rarely looks flustered.
Ted was a Spitfire pilot in World War 2 and as a very old man with a glint in his eye, he now runs the newsagent on the corner. He’s a lovely old man but he was a tyke in his younger day.
An older guy who is all fun-and-games until the shit hits the fan, at which point he tends to fall apart

Supremely organised, Telford keeps an up-to-date log book for his car and in a perfect world he'd like to have one for his pushbike too. Regimes of order and diligence: this is what Telford enjoys. Note that if he gets called 'Tele' then forget it, he's all over the place with too many friends and too much artistic fun to worry about any kind of order in his life, but not Telford. He wears a suit to work, is part of a strict hierarchy and doesn't mind poverty in the world, so long as he never sees it.

Tem doesn't just show up, although you might presume that by just looking at him. He asks questions when the time is right, he smiles at strangers, encouraging optimism where possible and he is inquisitive in the world. Does he slip under the radar a bit? Well, I suppose he does. He's certainly never so stressed that he can't sleep at night, and by and large his calming nature is appreciated by all and sundry. Nice work Tem.
His middle Asian origins are 1000’s of years old and it helps him to spread the word of peace. (An aggressive temper is something he never has.)

A light weight American name, and the title of any individual who gets frightened when someone leaves a door open at the other end of the house, thus allowing a chilly breeze to infiltrate the building.
Terrence secretly detests being called Terry, which some people do just to get a rise out of him. He likes fine wine and expensive restaurants, and he went grey very prematurely.

Okay, sure, once upon a time Terry rhymed with Unreliable and, sometimes, Downright Wrong, but his youthful exuberance came through with the goods. Who wants to grow up anyway? Isn't the world serious enough as it is? People like Terry are here to remind us these things, just don't get him too drunk at the Christmas Party - and if you do, film him. You'll be able to use the defamation evidence in court and it'll probably be funny.
By any definition Tex is the name of a rocket launch pad, and we know what that means.

And already I find myself with a stringent voice, speaking aloud, chest inflated, as if preparing an oration for the high council. 
"Oh Lord Titus, my name is Thaddeus, and I appear before you as a devilish and subversive rogue....."
In reality, of course, he throws tantrums and has the capacity to drive us all quite bonkers.
The method actor. Loves the stage. Loves Hamlet.
The local chief. If you want a decent guide to get you over those mountains and to the sea, beyond, then he's your man.

Theo, I know you’re a good guy. I know you do heaps around the house and I know you’ve got a good heart, but you can’t live with your mother until you’re 40. One day you’ve got to get out there and do it on your own, brother.

A staunch royalist. Whether he's English or not, if there is some major royal event happening on television - it might be a wedding, or an anniversary of sorts - Theodor will pull out his royal outfit, which makes him look like a silly kind of sailor, and sit in front of the television drinking cups of tea while grasping a small Union Jack flag. It's quite bizarre.

Perhaps not as zealous as his twin brother (Theodor), Theodore still manages to follow some ornate hobby with an obsessive level of intent. And yes, he loves dressing up to express his love of whatever it is he’s into. If he was into World War 2 army paraphernalia, for example, he would delight in dressing up like a humble corporal in the artillery regiment despite having never joined any military service. Likewise if he was nuts about his model train collection, he’d dress up like an old fashioned train driver. I think you get the picture.

Thiago walks like he's dancing, which means he's never unhappy, and his Brazilian heritage helps. Remember however that just because he's a dancing Brazilian man doesn't mean he doesn't think deeply or has noble ambitions. Last I heard he was studying corporate finance, or maybe it was environmental law? If it's the latter and he lives in Brazil, then they could really use his help.
Earnest and organised if he has no nickname, Thomas has a personality similar to that of a set of architect’s drawings for any modern office block.
Thommo is tall, friendly and industrious and just ever so slightly reserved.

Thompson was born about 70 years too late. Sadly, the days of chivalrous young men dressed in suits and wearing hats, smoking cigarettes and wooing ladies at dances as a trendy and fashionable thing to do are long past. It's a pity, eh? In a past life Thompson worked for RAF during WW2, in England, intelligence gathering. A refined man these days, he is still highly intelligent, he is awkward around fast women and he likes tinkering on his old Triumph sports car. Unfortunately, the bulk of what constitutes the modern life leaves him quite bored.
Indian giver.
Ironically, Tie is the last person to be tied down to a job, a woman or any kind of long-term obligation. Indeed, he is one free man.
A Tasmanian Devil, a North American wildcat or a British bulldog.

Too little to box and too large to be a jockey, Tighe might make an excellent gymist. He has energy to burn and he's quick on his feet and some encouragement, here, never goes astray. He's not the scholarly type.

Tim can be a sneaky little bastard or a genuine legend and, irrespective of which, he is highly intelligent and slides around all decisions quickly. By and large he has very good hand-eye coordination and you can be rest assured that once in his life, and only once, will he say to a fool who is pestering him, “You’re a mere apparition of humanity.”

(Pronounced Timmo) As Tim’s  more effervescent alter ego, Timo’ spends more time in the light, and has a greater propensity for absurd, unselfconscious fun. He’ll never run the country and that’s a shame because our world would be happier and far more playful if he did. 
Bravo, Timo’.

Timothy is an interesting chap. He's quick and he's clean, and he often stands in front of the mirror of a morning, pulls up his Y-front underpants very high around his waist and says, "Morning Timothy!" He has no problem standing naked in public.

No, he's not tiny and he's not tight with money either...well...unless you're outside the family or are a buffoon, which is fair enough. What Tino is, is organised, and he doesn't like surprises, even though he actually operates quite well under pressure. 
Ever seen the TV show M.A.S.H? Well had they found a taller bloke than Radar to play Radar, but who rarely got flustered and who was far more adept with the opposite sex then Tino would be your man. 
 
Note: Tino's mother sends him a hamper every week. It's just how it is.
On prima facie evidence there’s no way Tiran could have done it. He’s a dill, sure, but he’s not remotely evil.

No matter where he's from, Tito loves the USA because it's the only 'civilised' country on earth where you can walk off the street and buy a gun. (Note from Management: Tito, take it back and don't be a fucking idiot.)

If you want to find T.J on any Saturday afternoon, you need look no further than the betting ring at the local horse races where he can be seen staring up at the latest odds, frowning hard at how he's going to approach the next race.

Tobias is not a spectator. He participates because he’s curious and because he wants to help propagate love, peace and humour in the world. True story. Hang shit on him if you want to, but react not when he looks at you like you’re an idiot. For him to do so means you are.
Kiwi’s aren’t normal and it’s for this reason that the world barely tolerates them but Tobin is different. Is he the most normal, sane and well-rounded of them all?

A puny lizard that drops its tail at the first sign of danger, before scurrying back into the undergrowth leaving a trail of blood, fear and goo. (Ironically, perhaps, the only really potent Tobys are completely gay.)
You’ll never see him in an office and you may not see him standing in the one spot for too long, either. Boats, deserts, exotic women....these are the kinds of things that Toci finds fascinating.
Todd rhymes with Oops. Not in a catastrophic way, mind you, more in the, I-forgot-to-feed-the-cat-but-now-that-I’ve-remembered-I-will, kind of way.

While rarely a genius, Tom is a truly good person who is ideal in his role as a big protective brother. (Unless he is unusually small in stature, in which case it’s a different story, and one that tells of speed and ambition.)
Head waiter at a five star silver service restaurant. Long fingers and good nails.

Haunted by the demons of self-doubt, Tommy throws himself into life in an attempt to combat them, head on. He sports more bruises on his body than anyone and large, complex business issue are difficult for him to get his head around.

Tono has seen all the Twilight movies three times and he desperately wants to be able to turn himself into a giant werewolf whenever he wants so he can meet girls like whats-her-name. (He's got her poster on his bedroom wall.)

It’s often difficult to know what’s going on behind the eyes. He could be a great bloke who is honest and friendly and thoughtful, then again he might be a tall sleazy strip of pelican shit. The more outgoing Tony is, however, the more he tends towards the latter. See how you go...
Tor keeps it simple ‘cause he can. His name evokes images of Scandinavian fjords, smooth running Harley Davidsons and boyish charms, and this is no mean feat.

It's hard to utter Torben's name with a giant smile on your face and so there a certain sense of gravitas conveyed to the man. Is he serious in adulthood? Well, he certainly has that potential, but the trade off is a staunch work ethic. If Torben ever goes off the rails he probably doesn't do it mildly, although the constrictive nature of his name will largely avoid this. Educated, of strong opinion and well-groomed are some of the things people remember about young Torben but make no mistake, Torben has high moral standards and he is kind. Don't forget that.

Toristen puts forward a coherent argument every time. As a barrister with some style he is garnishing a reputation around town. Sure, he's full of it and loves the sound of his own voice, but this kind of ego comes with the territory.

We understand that he is from Earth but not much more than that. What we do know is that he is hilariously funny, even if he’s doing something as banal as boiling himself an egg, although no one is sure where he is going or how he intends to get there. At some point we expect he will cease living and this will be a sad day...

In the same lineage as Trent and the late James Coburn, Torren is a man whose natural ease and charisma opens most doors quite magically. 
Does he work hard? We have no idea but we doubt it. 
Do the ladies adore him? Yes they do, and if Torren is a gay man then the men adore him even more.
Is he an outdoor, water-kind-of-guy?
If he’s not he should be. 
And his mum loves him more than the rest of her children. (It’s just how it is.) 
The End.
Torrin is a doer and a thinker. Rarely incapacitated, Torrin often holds back his more extreme emotions for those times when the crowd is somewhere else.

It's not that Tory sticks to a tight schedule, on the surface he's not that organised, but his light footedness and his propensity to not sit still for very long means he gets quite a bit done without even meaning to. Basically, if he's being slack you hardly notice, which in turn means he can be quite slack for most of the time. It helps that he has an infectious grin. Generally the girls love him.

Nimble on his feet and dextrous with his hands, Tosawi is deeper than his affable smile lets on. Then again, maybe that's his little secret. He has the capacity to keep things very simple. All he does, in order to achieve this, is act with a good heart at all times. Yeah, it can't always be like this, I mean, shit, he's not a priest or anything, but his path in life is clear cut and uncluttered. Honesty of words and actions will get you a long way. Indeed, it'll get you ALL the way. Tosawi.

A little one-dimensional, but it’s not his fault. Until they meet him people don’t believe Toto actually exists. The result is a warm, affable man who'd take a bullet for just about anyone. He’s not a corporate heavy weight.
The Storm Chaser - either meteorological or internal.

Yeah, yeah, he's heard all the jokes, trust me. What Trace is, however, is patient, self-confident and quite funny. He was brought up with the capacity to think on his feet and as a very interested person these days, he won't just divvy out his friendship and his time willy nilly.
The quiet type. Some people are just better working alone.

Tracy is liberal man and a liberal thinker, but he's neither wasteful, slovenly or overtly rude. Yes, occasionally strangers are perplexed when they meet a man and not the woman they anticipated, but this surprise provides Tracy with something of an open window to express what he wants and who he is. Rarely are those strangers let down. Consequently, Tracy was never really destined to think one-dimensionally.
The Loving Bulldozer.
Travis is harmless enough but he’s a bit silly.

The dealer and shaker who looks beyond the surface of things to try and understand what's really going on. Yep, his lady is begging for him to add-on to the back deck, but no way would Treeve do it himself. He can afford a good carpenter, so that's who he'll hire to do it. Fuck it, he might even nick off to Japan for a quick ski holiday while it's being done. No point sitting around here, trying to talk to traders and the crew in the know with all that racket going on outside. Treeve is a happy guy, but he likes his space, and he likes things organised. Don't waste his time by asking him to come over and help fix your fence.

Trehan is one of the few men who would perform very well as a mother. No, it's not a gay/feminine reference, more an expression of his capacity to care and watch over those younger people who are either in his charge or around him, in general. Does he have eyes in the back of his head? Almost. Trehan is a careful organiser who likes nice shoes.

A suit and tie kind of guy. And that's great, until he finds himself on a tram, train, bus or ferry on the way to work, looking down at himself to discover he's forgotten his trousers and is standing in only a pair of underpants. Trenam, a word of advice: ditch the suit, brother. It was never really you in the first place.

Tall, blonde and invariably lean from the early years of hard work or hard playing, Trent lives the good life - copywriter, art critic or charter boat skipper - and these days he’s a relaxed character who is enjoying life to the full.
In high school he was first in class every time. It was nearly embarrassing.

Trev is a happy kind of a gumby who manages to hold it all together, usually, and who rarely injures himself, as well as keeping the vehicle in a straight line no matter how much it's raining. The key is to not panic and we may well write this on his gravestone. And no, he's not going anywhere for a while. He's destined to be an old and much loved man. Thanks Trev.

No, he's not a bloody trevally, you fool, he's a human, and quite a bizarre one, actually.

Why's that?

Well, look at him. Fuck knows where he bought those green velour trousers from but they're a foot too long, which is a pity because you should see his shoes!

I can't even see his face for hair.

I know. Me neither.

What does he do?

Hah, that's the funny bit. Would you believe me if I told you he's never worked a day in his life?

Yes, I think I would. Did he inherit lots of money?

Mmmm.....I don't know. No one knows. He's got a great stereo though, so perhaps he was a DJ?

Ungainly around women and deceptively serious, in general, Trevor never loses sight of his mantra that a fair reward is gained from a fair effort in all aspects of life that matter; food, friendship and construction.
Trey has learned to confront his fears. It took a while, but it means he now strides through the world doing what he wants without any sense of falseness, guilt or laziness.

Yep, Tricky by name and cheeky by nature, Tricky arrives on the party scene with a reputation and an ego, neither of which you want to miss. And yes, in his younger day, and possibly not even in his younger day, Tricky was a kinky little fucker with a plethora of friends who were more than happy to stoke the fire. None of this shy, quiet and demure bullshit here folks. Tricky is here for this moment we’re standing in, so just strap yourself in (or strap one up), brace yourself for a rockin’ good time and simply jump. At the very least the associated laughter and hubbub which surrounds Tricky will cheer you up. 

The End.
Never heard of the Old Testament, and wouldn’t pay any heed to anyone who did. Trimmer is a fit, busy business man, and he rarely takes his problems home.
At the moment of orgasm he yells out, “OH TRISTAN!!! TRISTAN!! GO, TRISTAN, GO!!”
Miraculously, Tristram is the only person to yell louder than his close relation, Tristan. Except Tristram yells out, "OH JOYOUS TRISTRAM! HERE ART THOU MOMENT, YOUNG MAN!!"

Trong plays the bugle and he only knows one way to play: LOUD. He’s tried to play quietly - say, when he's practising late at night - but he's just too passionate about his craft. Go you good thing, Trong!
Troy breastfed until he was 23 yrs old and this has screwed with his head something chronic.
Attends Star Trek conferences.

Really? Tsunami, no offence but your parents are fools. At least they didn’t call you Sandstorm or Tornado, I suppose. Either way, Tsunami can only be a quiet and humble fellow because there is literally no where else for him to go. He has warm eyes and a warm handshake, and he’s no rockstar. What did you want Mum and Dad? For him to end up in fucking jail?
Round body. Big round smile. Another perpetual young man who rarely does ill in the world. Too nice for politics and not fit enough to spear-fish, he'd make an excellent wine critic.

Yeah I know, you wouldn't imagine him to be the world's most adaptive strategist would you? We certianly didn't. And no, the only six-pack he's ever seen is the one he tends to pull out of the fridge, plonk in the esky and take down to the jetty with the rest of his fishing gear.

A wanna-be jockey who grew too big by far. You can still him at the racetrack, though. He's the bloke with the syringe, going around and injecting all the horses with the special elixir that makes them run faster.

Coke dealer. And no, we're not talking about the drink. How the cops haven't got him yet no one knows. He's always smiling and he never seems to conceal what he does for a living. Perhaps that's why he gets away with it?
Into yoga and meditation. Vegetarian.

The name of a completely tame, albeit very rare New Zealand black bear. Yep, he weighs 400kg and he could snap your neck without so much as thinking about it, and he'd probably even quite enjoy eating you if the thought ever occurred to him, but not this guy. He's been surrounded with too much love and attention from when he was a cub. The only thing he would do is snap the neck of anyone or anything trying to harm those he loved, and he's too happy and relaxed to get upset about anything else, so long as he gets his tucker. Tupou.
Everyone thinks he’s on drugs.

Twiggy doesn’t seem to be that bright and he doesn’t seem to have that much common sense but he’s a humorous bloke who, once in a while, comes out with these little gems that literally stops everyone in their tracks. It might be an observation or an idea, but they’re worth waiting for. So perhaps he’s not a total dill after all…

Ty is caught between a rock and a hard place. Society, you see, attempts to brainwash all of us into working hard and pursuing material goals that amount to nothing in the end, really, but people like Ty are almost impossible to get through to, and that's a good thing. For instance, how can you expect a man to dedicate himself to maximising a profit margin when even the meer thought of hooning down a flying fox through a rain forest gets him frothing at the mouth: Ty.
Tye would love to fly by the seat of his pants and he gets as close as being a good driver when he's sober. If he were a ship he wouldn't leak much.

Option A:  Tyler spent two years in a rehab clinic trying to kick a cocaine habit that cost him his family and most of his friends. These days he can be seen begging for money near the entrance to most train stations, but it was never his fault.

Option B:  Tyler has barely worked a full day in his life, and it must be said that someone shouldn’t, otherwise where are the differences in life? Having said that, it wouldn’t kill him, and as a product of the modern generation he seems to have one eye permanently fixed on the bloody mirror/smartphone screen.
Tynan suffers from having well-to-do parents that don't push him. Tynan, I'm sure you know this, but you MUST test yourself, whether you think you're ready for it or not.
Goes outside to fart.

An usual man. He's no namby-pamby that's for sure. Tyree listens to what people have to say, making a judgement call only then. He's only really dangerous if he gets bored. Is he dyslexic? I only ask that because it seems he's not reading enough.

Tryon is an excellent adjudicator. Yes, he likes to muck around and hang shit on his friends as much as the next person, and he can take it as well as give it, but out of all his bunch he will be the first to speak up when someone or something has gone too far. He will therefore stick up for the underdog if need be. Thank you Tyron.

He may be a steroid-sucking gym-freak, a 150kg melted-cheese legend or the local city council mayor who spends $1500 of taxpayers’ money, each week, on ladies’ of the night, but whatever he does and whoever he does it with, Tyrone operates out there on the fringes.

Tyson is a gem. He is the lad at the playground that will try and swing on a monkey bar that is covered in vegetable oil. He is therefore deceptively thoughtful because the harder he hangs on, the quicker he slips off.

Is he Palestinian? Is he even an earthling? Last time we saw him he was wearing high-heels and rabbit ears, and for a sexually and artistically diverse organism we expect it, I think. Ubee is also one of the kindest and most generous people you will ever meet.

A silver-haired businessman who gives due where it's warranted, quickly disregarding those people and situations where it isn't. He can't help looking a little calous in his behaviours. One or some of his parents were German or Swiss, and what can you do?

Hard work - has he heard of it? Does he pick up after himself, even at 30 years of age? Having been blacklisted by many girls in the early days, we're hoping he's learnt a few lessons about civility and politeness. And he's great at spending other people's money 

(Note: If Urijah is rather shy then he is the exact opposite, and presents as a pinnacle of love and compassion.)

Hey? What are you saying?....Usain, you say?....Well, Christ, he's got to be happy, as in, happy all the time, right? And you can't be happy all the time without travelling plenty, yeah? And you can't be travelling plenty without occasionally being late for the airport, eh? So, here then, is the happiest man you'll meet, who's always heading as fast as he can towards somewhere, be it an airport, a girl's bedroom or the nearest ATM. Amen.
Frizzy hair. Outstanding energy. He shadow boxes whenever he’s standing in any kind of queue.
Usman is a tranquil man who deals with pressure very well because he has very clear picture in his head of what he wants and where he is headed.
Uwe, pronounced Oove, is a fascinating sticky beak who, like Rove and De Shan before him, is ostensibly unembarrasable. And yes, like Fergus and Laurina he's got some wonderful kinks.
Valdis has the occasionally annoying knack of systematising everything. It's drives his children batty, along with his long-suffering wife.
Poker face. He has a very tight set of close friends and even they will tell you that Van is hard to crack into.

Vance dances like a robot in that he doesn't like getting has arms and hands too far from his body. It's all about keeping things in line, with Vance. He's a reserved kind of bloke and like most cats he'll relax once he gets familiar with  you.

For a name which sounds like it belongs on the side of an interplanetary rocket ship, Vander is a surprisingly mellow cat. Self-conscious, even. His friends can’t seem to do without him, and women move towards him as if empowered by some kind of subtle, lateral gravity. The whole career-thing is his only issue, mostly because decision making isn’t his best card. He’d much prefer to go with the proverbial flow.

Talk about white line fever. Varian steps off a plane at some foreign airport and it's like magic dust has been sprinkled over him. Sometimes he even changes his name. But all of it aims to rid him of the personality he is loaded with back home so he can explode out into the ether and become the quintissential, Masked Avenger!

Vasco is a slick and super-smart Real Estate agent in either the Gold Coast or Miami. He wears a fat gold chain around his right wrist that matches the one around his neck, he drives a Mercedes convertible and he wouldn’t change his lot in life if you paid him, which is something that you wouldn’t have to do, anyway.
What is it about loud, laughing, demonstrative Greek men? After a while you just want them to leave, yet you can't help but watch and smile at the show. Vasilios.
Maurizio's business partner. They are famous in the nightclubs of Miami, the Gold Coast, Australia, and certain parts of Mexico City.
Vassilis retired when he hit 25. Sure, he plagiarised that first plot a little, because when there’s a corner to cut he’ll cut it. His theory is that in 100 years he’ll be dead so why will it matter?

Vaughan is six feet tall, wears big black sunglasses, a cheap suit (the trousers of which are four inches too short) and is a surprisingly good used-car salesman. He doesn’t like ripping off grannies but he can’t help it. They’re just too easy.
Vaughn, I know the spelling is different but that's okay. You and your kindred spirit arrive from the same egg so please check out Vaughan, above, and enjoy the ride.
The Song of India.
If you are happy and active you will always succeed - this is his mantra. If you’re going to hang out with Veejay there is an 80% probability that the rule book will be thrown out, and rightly so.

You know the dream you have when you’re suddenly standing in a crowded restaurant or maybe in class, and you’re completely naked? Well, psycho-analysts in the 60’s coined that the Vernon Dream. I’ve no idea why.

The short name hides a complex individual. If Vic is bad he’s nasty but if he’s good he’s great. Whichever one he is, however, he prefers the outdoor life, usually, and he’s pretty good with most types of engines, and even though he sports a beer gut.
Victor is the name of a gold plated calligraphy pen that’s worth thousands, and who looks excellent when sticking out the top of a breast pocket.
The Artistic Director.

Vigal always looks kind of silly sitting in an office. He needs a cause to fire him up, you see. Plonk him in a cubicle and tell him he has to wear a tie and all the air will be sucked out of him immediately. It might even kill him.
Always has a form guide in his pocket and never sits down for longer than 7 minutes.

All Vincents are ultra-sensitive souls who wrestle with their own substantial talents and personalities from the minute they draw first breathe. Often overcome with emotion, it’s no wonder Van Gough cut his own ear off and topped himself.
The Glib Parasite.

Heralding from the same bloodline as Eugene and Herman, Virgil is anything but conventional. Yes, he is full of love and yes, he is a patient and compassionate man, but it's his playful ridiculousness that really warms the crowd. Ever seen the opening sequence of a television show called F-Troop, when Captain Palmenter is accidentally riding backwards on his horse? Well this kind of accidental but brilliantly conceived (by the gods) stunt is called A Virgil. Planet Earth therefore would be a much sadder place without him, and amen to that.
The subtle patriarch who doesn’t mind cutting corners, and who congratulates those who do when things turn out well. He’s never quite so agreeable if they don’t, however.

What a perfectly humorous and gentle individual. True, there are one or two Vivians who, due to their surroundings, have needed to become incredibly tough and dangerous, but let me tell you these specimens are rarely spotted in the wild. Your stock-standard Vivian is rarely short, he is a reader, he is a thinker, and he has odd, albeit, harmless hobbies - like collecting teaspoons for instance. It all just adds another part of the puzzle that IS Vivian.

Vlad is the kind of man who will insist he's a really funny guy while he's got a revolver aimed at the middle of your forehead. 
“Yeah, Vlad, you’re fuckin’ hilarious mate,” is the general response.

Authentic and eager without being effusive, Von is skilled at devising a framework around a problem or a situation and then seeing it executed. And he has a wicked sense of humour (when he’s not working).

Vosso always struggles in business because he does more than what he says he's going to do. I know, we didn't anticipate that either up here in the commentary box. Vosso, a word of advice: give from a position of power, not from a position of weakness. That way you benefit as well.
Fairy floss, my arse. Vossy is a competitor and don't let the comfy sounding name give you the wrong impression. The heat of battle is where he does his best work.
Vrasidas leads by example.

Sure, most Wades are builders until they realise they have a lot more fun staying at home and seeing how much pain they can inflict upon themselves by squashing their own hand in a vice. If that's the case then this Wade might even baits dogs for a hobby. However, a mutated set of Wade genes often produces the funniest man in, not just the room, but the whole damn building. I hope you're dealing with the latter. Management.

Wah will have a crack at anything, and he’ll do it with good intention. For instance, the first time he took acid he ended up out on the street in broad daylight and when he began to feel as though his clothes were made of bugs he stripped naked and wound up totally lost. He climbed up a tree to try and escape the bugs on the ground, until he spotted an old man whom he hoped might tell him where he was. Wah jumped down, all smiles, until the old fellow began belting his naked buttocks with his walking stick. Writhing on the ground in agony and pleading for mercy, Wah was actually delighted when the cops showed up because the paddy wagon they put him in felt like a giant, cool living room, plus no one was beating him. They didn’t even charge him.
Wal likes his meat and three veg for dinner followed by a bowl of ice-cream. He volunteers for the emergency services.
Like Merlin the Magician, Waldemar is the textbook eccentric genius.
Waleed is well-oiled, be it philosophically, spiritually, socially and financially. He might even be a little too well-oiled.
As the genial head of the local APEX or Rotary branch, Wally is filled with the deeds of goodness that are misguided only 10% of the time.
Bloody funny. Very clever.
Abused by his wife, Walter speaks very slowly and after orgasm, which is a rare event in itself, he often can’t speak for days.
In a past life Ward was an SS officer in the Third Reich, so he's got a bit to catch up on when it comes to unconditional love. He's making progress though…

“Hello, I’m Warne,” he says, quietly. 
Immediately everyone is looking for a punchline, but it doesn’t come. Warne is a calm, unassuming and purposeful man and there it is.
See Kylie, although he is way less dignified.

As a variety of ferret, Warren is industrious and crafty. After some initial weirdness, he is usually quite loveable but if you corner him or freak him out too much, he’s liable to start smelling odd and he might have a go at you. Not the most nostalgic of creatures.
A muscle bound twit who specializes in verbal diarrhoea and offending women

Highly educated (he finished primary school) Warwick still has trouble doing up his shoe laces so they stay done up. Why is that Warwick? We hope that it's not used as a ploy to stare up girls' skirts Warwick. It's not, is it? (Would we credit it? Sadly, yes we would.)
Watto' hates eating at restaurants because it means he has to use a knife and fork. He's much happier with a meat pie and no shoes.

Waylon, you do understand of course that you and you alone construct your reality? So, for a friendly and relaxed fellow, what are you complaining about? 

(Although, can you blame him? His name is one of the few which can be said while one is asleep, which thus imbibes him with a sense that, really, he need not actually do anything in life.....Maybe buy a horse and feed it? That might just about do it as a hobby.)

Option A: An ingrown toenail that’s red and swollen, painful to look at and even less fun to deal with when kicked. 

Option B: Of humble stock, his parents gave him that rather rural name in the hope he’d work hard and make something of himself. Did he? Well, you’d be surprised. Yes, many-a-Wayne slipped through the gaps and never got to rise up, but some Waynes used the force of their good heart to successfully propel themselves forward. 

(Note: The only real hiccup for both species is that they are hindered by the absence of the gene which enables a human to comprehend modern digital technology. Although, who knows? Perhaps it’s actually a blessing…)

That line from the Bible should have read: "Bless those that carry a young heart like Wayno, for they are the ones to be emulated and they are the ones that will - and should - inherit the earth. Amen."
Sweet-natured, reliable and irreverent, Wazza lives for embarking on adventures with his friends.
Never underestimate Webby. His simplicity is actually cohesion, not confusion.
Welchy gets injured all the time and frowns whenever he’s in pain, which is quite a lot, unfortunately, but he is a fun-loving legend who lives his life in his jocks.

(Ancestor of Bruce.) Back in the dark ages, in Europe, invading forces would attempt to bust open the gates of a castle with a giant log carried by twenty men or more, who would slam it repeatedly against them. In the absence of any smashing device, however, they’d just grab Wendell, pick him up side-on, and crunch his tremendously large and dense cranium against the gates, instead. It never really bothered Wendell because all he knew of it was a rather loud knocking noise.

A big, round South African beetle who pushes the other bugs out of the way in order to get to the pollen/sugar/dung heap first. And when he gets there he engorges himself to obesity with the expectation that this massive increase in body fat is will attract females for miles. (Wentzel, that’s great, but you should probably wipe your face before you embark on the hunt for a mate, mate.)

Wes is a big bloke. He knows how to fight a fire, he’s familiar with nearly every part of most old cars, he’s handy with a welder, he can defend himself, he makes people laugh and at the end of a long day, or even during an annual local festival, he loves a good, cold beer. Howdy Wes.
The Wesley Treatment is what happens to anything – sandwiches and packs of soft drink cans, for example – when it is wrapped tightly in clear plastic film.

Yep, he's definitely out there, all right. Not the academic type, West is his own man who trusts his decisions and not for a moment would he heed advice from someone he didn't respect - unless it involved some perilous task, chore or adventure he didn't know much about. Women adore him, partly because of his looks, but mostly because he exudes an untameable, dangerous vibe. West.
Often wearing a high-viz shirt or jacket, Weston is a working man and a cheeky one. His needs are simple and his friendship is genuine, which is a common theme amid the working class.

Extremely difficult to take down, be it philosophically, physically or emotionally, Westy is one step ahead of the game. He rarely takes work stresses home with him. Hang on, hang on…actually, that's a good point. Does he work??
Weylin hasn't dusted around his house since before his wife left him, and that was way back in the 60's, not long before he shot his horse through insanity. (His, not the horses.)
(If only he was so lucky.) Whacky is intelligent and methodical.

You'd hope that the only way a man is called Whitney is because his surname is Houston. In which case Whitney can barely wipe the smile from his face, no matter what he's doing. Indeed, the more he is called Whitney, the more fun he seems to have. And he isn't little.
The name of a woollen tea cosie that hippies put on their head at dance festivals.

Not prone to flaunting it in public, Wilco is far more subversive and cool. He's the sort of bloke who is worth millions behind the scenes, but is actually more content in some simple life which contains the bare essentials. Rarely manic or in-your-face angry, he moves in line with things called gravity and momentum. As the Buddhists say, life should be like pouring water down hill, and this sums up Wilco nicely. (Yes, this might mean he is occasionally seen as lazy, such is life.)

One can envisage Wilder reclining on a Chesterfield sofa, smoking a Cuban with one hand and swirling a brandy with the other, trying to ignore some bullshit as spoken by an ill-informed idiot about peak oil and it's imminent, theoretical impact on Wilder's rather expansive share portfolio, which, by the way, he attained through guile, a natural desire to take the odd risk and a general belief that all money markets are just a game. 

Certainly, ain't nothing too crazy about Wilder, ladies and gentlemen, but he does tend to succeed.

Wilfred accepts the odd kick-back with a shrug of his shoulders. As the CEO of a large, successful company who has come to realise that life is something of a silly game, he's done his fair share of hard work and now understands life can't be taken too seriously. So, yes, he has had hookers under his desk performing deeds we can't talk about here while at the same time interviewing people in front of him. On the other hand, he's given millions away to charities who need help. Such is Wilfred.

Will is almost too nice for his own good. He was a textbook student in his younger day and in adulthood he rushes to the aid of all and everyone. He makes an excellent grief counsellor, school teacher or ambulance driver.
Willem slides underneath the surface like a large and able Eagle Ray. He moves easily, stealthily, almost, and he doesn't really get involved with predictable life paths.

A sage who has seen and done it all; war, love, family, everything. Now that he’s an old man he likes to sit outside in the morning sun, where he reads the paper and quietly reminisces about his wonderful life that is coming to a close.
A well-intended drip.
A good friend and possible work colleague of Solomon.

Wilson opens his front door each morning on the way to work or where ever, and some tiny part of him always expects his minions to be there to greet him, frothing at how excited they are to behold his greatness. They're never there of course, but he likes the idea...

Winslow is a big guy who is very hard to take down, either because of his actual physical size or his constant massive grin, and both are equally undeniable on a person. It helps that Winslow is almost certain to have a large chunk of islander DNA in him and once he starts laughing it infects the entire village. Nice work Winslow.

Option A: Winston walks into the shed where his friend is working, careful not to cut himself on anything while he looks around curiously.
"What's this thing?" he asks, picking up a strange looking implement he's never seen before.
His friend looks at him and smiles. "Winston, it's a hammer, mate. We use them to hit these things called nails."
"Oh, yes," Winston says earnestly. "I know that. I mean, what I meant to say was, how long have you had it?"

Option B: An indigenous elder who has scars on his body and face from initiation ceremonies, many years ago. He talks to the dead and he even sees the future sometimes. You don't wanna do wrong by Winston and his kin for he might even point the bone, and if he does it will be well-deserved.
It's not snowing in your jocks is it, mate? No? Good, then smile and stop trying to look and act cool. Where’s the fun in that? Girls prefer a smile anyway.
Wiremu is either married to, or the brother of, a girl called Tuhi. Neither of them are particularly normal.

Unathletic. Wise lives on his game pad, his tablet or in front of his computer screen. Wise, some advise from management: you're a smart, funny indivudual so get outside and throw out thy evil devices! Use that body of yours before it's too late. Run. Jump. Get a skateboard and ride it down a freeway. Parachute. We don’t care, just do something. But most important, TRAVEL, AND TALK TO EVERYONE YOU MEET. That's where the real fun is.
Woggy = Flash Gordon.

Pronounced Voy-tek, he is his own man all right, in every situation. Uncompromising and reasonably unforgiving, Wojtek, don’t take this the wrong way, but can we suggest you lighten-the-fuck up? (His Eastern European heritage however means there might only be a small chance of that happening.)
The black sheep.
Petrochemical engineer/biochemist/geologist/meteorologist.

I think most of us in this room acknowledge Woodrow is never going to be the fastest member of the team, but that isn't his job. As a brilliant strategist, Woodrow looks likes he's barely moving, and this brings us to a salient point. His success isn't a fluke, and it can be put down to two things: 

1: He mysteriously knows where the ball is going to be in about 20 minutes time.

2: As a gifted lateral thinker with a calm persona, when the plan he's concocted doesn't come to fruition, he'll constantly adapt and plot without so much as a frown on his ample forehead, which means all those watching think that he's planned the whole thing anyway.
Woody is rock solid and another comic genius. He loves women and he loves his life.
Woolfy is that cheeky prick who itches for a bit of chaos.
Megolamaniac.

Ever seen that ad for Corona? I think it's set in Mexico. You know the one - three blonde, surf hippies are each sitting on a box of Corona stubbies, beer in hand, and they're looking out to a sunset-lit surf break where someone is carving it up. Wylie may or may not be the bloke on the wave, but he's definitely one of the dudes sitting on one of the Corona boxes, enjoying an ale, laughing with some gorgeous surf-girl, and contemplating dinner and a doobie afterwards. Wylie.
The prophylactic used by men of distinction.

And he does too, but never by using brute force or stand-over tactics. Wyn prevails by being dedicated and persistent, and by having a passion for what he does. As a matter of fact, if he’s really concentrating he’s almost unapproachable. Not out of rudeness you understand, but just because great devotion and attention to detail requires maximal attention. (And, predictably, he always builds a loving, tight family.) 
Nice one Wyn.

The name of that harmless, shiny little pony that kiddies ride on at the show, on the merry-go-round. As a pixie in a previous life, he's working up to be store-front mannequin in the next one, before he steps into the realm of a fully-fledged human after that. And he'll get there too and we're lucky to have him because Xander hasn't got an evil bone in his body.
A private school boy and all round nice guy. He won’t set the world on fire but he won’t bore us to death either. Probably.

A proactive kid and a forward-thinking man. Set-backs, yep, we all have them, but sadly few of us realise they’re actually springboards to greatness, for later on. It’s just how it is and Yadin is all over it.

To suggest Yadran is calculated is to do the man a disservice. Yes, he's a staunch competitor and he hates, hates, hates coming last, but a sense of humour is never far away. For example, having not sat over a chess board for 15 years or so, he is the sort of fellow who, when asked out of the blue by a young nephew if he'd like a game, is not only delighted at seeing first-hand how a young man he loves is progressing, he will be flooded with the glorious memories of what playing chess does to his brain. Most notably, it's the hidden strategy that he missed (which, to a lesser extent he's applied to his own life) and the notion of cornering your opposition through a greater intelligence. (In reality, of course, he'll let his nephew beat him every third game.)
Chinese herbalist. No matter what ailment he's told of and no matter how grim the forecast for a person, you'll rarely see him without a smile. Everything is connected, he'll tell you. Everything.
My god, what a great big dollop of over-the-top romantic fluff and carry-on is he. Yanni, why didn’t you ever get yourself off to acting school? Although it’s never too late, eh?
A big, hairy Greek man whose eyebrows have melded into one giant, black snake. He's as soft and as cuddly as a seven foot toy teddy bear.

The fridge stopped working? The dingy sprung a leak? The fan belt broke out in the middle of nowhere?
Fear not. Yash will leap into action, making a joke at every turn while he does his darndest to fix the problem, usually employing completely unorthodox methodology. 
Success rate: 78% 
(as opposed to his romantic success rate: 83%)

Is Yens a dishwasher technician with a German heritage? Well, certainly, of all the people in the Kingdom who could perform at this job admirably there are very few out there who could do it better. No, he doesn’t laugh at meaningless jokes but he is a fabulous, upstanding, loyal man and he oozes technical competence no matter what he’s into. Not a fingernail biter. Yens.

Yoey approaches life like a skimming stone that is 4-bounces into a perfect 9-bounce performance. 
Question: What’s possible?
Answer:  Everything.
……..suuuuuuuuure, he is! He's not that deep.
Yong performs autopsies in the name of forensic science.
Yoshi is something of a marvel. If a moment of possible humour and love presents itself Yoshi acts without thinking and the results are stupendous. It's a lesson for each of us, actually.
The Jungle Party organiser.

Where do you begin? What could take hours we’ll boil down to this: Give him his violin or his grand piano (a good one), or whatever musical/creative medium blows his hair back, stand back and just let him do his thing. He loves what he does and tears of joy have been known to be shed by onlookers.

If you think Youcef is useless you can leave the room for he is a dedicated, animated liver of life whose courage and honour could teach many within the Kingdom a valuable lesson or two. His only real fault, if you can call it that, is that he might occasionally smother people with love.

Youssef is a staunch-but-fair competitor. Never effusive, well, unless he is watching his son or daughter play soccer, Youssef is a friendly and committed chump who gallops through life with a smile stuck to the front of his head. He only frowns if, and when, people don’t do what they say they are going to do. Youssef commits and he expects you to commit as well. The End.

The textbook Russian spy. Very intelligent and with a high tolerance to pain, Yuri is a very direct person. Fascinating too, once you get to know him, and entertaining for that matter. Indeed, Yuri is good value, just make sure you read the “Safe Handling Methods” handbook for Yuri, beforehand.

Zac is the name of a bright red balloon at a birthday party that was full of air about 7 hrs ago, but now has a few slack wrinkles all over it. A nice guy. A nice balloon. Zac is (and was) a splendid mischief maker and when it counted he was very good. Barely a malicious bone in his body.
You know that thing chickens do after you lop their heads off? It's called the Zacarih Dance, and luckily you don't need to be Einstein to do it.

The poor bastard. His parents gave him that name because they thought it would be a cool thing to do, but they might as well have called him Seventy Cents Worth of Chips, as no one can ever take him seriously.

Yep, you might want to check out Zachary, Zachery. What was ommitted in his description however, and it applies to you too, is that you are both decent, happy young men. So well done on that front, anyway.
Fruit juice. 100% organic with no added sugar.

Serious? Zackary? Don't be bloody stupid. The last job interview he turned up to he wore a pale blue safari suit. He didn't really want the job of course, and so dressed in a way that he hoped would convince his potential employers at the accounting firm that he was slightly batty. It totally back-fired. They thought his colour and verve implied a certain kind of joie de vivre, and that he'd bring a breath of fresh air into the office. They employed him on the spot. Now he has to work a 9 to 5 job and doesn't he love it? Not! Although, his employers were right. He has definitely freshened up the place and people are happier with him around.

Quiet and care-free, Zade generally lets the girl make the first move but we have no idea about the direction of his life. When he begins to move toward some ambition or other can you let us know? Thanks. Management.
No, he's not a Greek symbol in mathematics. He's a polite and independent young man who quite unconcsiously endeavours to keep his life simple.
"Come on, hurry up! Give me that adrenalin, quick!.......Zaiden, are you awake? You need to go to school, mate. Wake up."…….
He's not the leader but he's definitely a member of the gang.
Zak looks quite manly but he is putty in the hands of any woman.

Loveable and completely unconventional, Zamika is always relaxed, and no matter how stressed or panicked those around him appear to be. It’s a product of having an unyielding sense of humour, courtesy of a ridiculous mother, combined with an ingrained sense of wrong and right.
As the world’s most honest snake charmer, Zan loves a challenge.

“Hang on, hang on,” the army Major says to the General. “You're going to put Zanda in charge of the mission into that Sudanese strong-hold? Are you out of your mind? Do you remember how he won the war games battle? He hired a bunch of girls and got them to put on bikinis, before sneaking them into the opposing forces HQ tent. What do you think you're doing? He doesn't take responsibility for himself and he'll get everyone killed!” The General smiles and picks up his drink, takes a sip and places it back on the table.
“Major,” he says, “this is Africa, and this is a wild part of the world. Do you think normal operational procedures are going to work here? I tell you, if Zanda does his job well he'll absolutely prevail, no one will get shot and he might even end up becoming a local warlord. Then, peace will be ours. I don't care how he does it.”
Zandah is a slightly watered-down version of his twin brother, Zanda, so you better go check him out. The pointless 'h' at the end of his name is the culprit, but that's another story.
A respectful young man who rarely shouts at people. Indeed, confrontations aren't really his thing and he'll go to huge lengths to avoid these situations, be it a public setting or not.

Zane is the name of an expensive pane of glass in a plush modern apartment. He lets in all the winter sun and keeps out the summer heat, and all that, and he does it pretty easily. And he looks good. Yep. That’s about it. He looks good.

Can you imagine Zatlin training for the infantry? On gattling gun training day he’d get on the thing, point it straight up into the sky and let go with everything, disregarding both his screaming sergeant, barely audible above the din, as well as the target at the end of the paddock that he’s supposed to be shooting at. When the ammo runs out, ending everyone’s day early, smoke is coming off the death machine, the sergeant is fuming and Zatlin is beaming the biggest smile anyone has ever seen. “Can you imagine what that’d look like at night?” he asks, looking up at the sky and wondering where all those machine gun bullets are right now. His sergeant looks at him and then points back to the barracks. “Son, I’m kicking you out of the army.”
Let’s face it, is a win-win for everyone.

We suspect all this predictive text rubbish is the cause, but phenotypic spelling is rapidly taking over the world – I mean, just look at L_ah’s parents – but Zavier’s folks did a bit better than hers.
