You see, (8) accused (6) of being a hypocrite because (6) just selected a living crayfish from the tank they’d like killed and cooked for their dinner, and according to (8), (6) raves on about the mistreatment and debasement of animals by human beings quite a bit. Anyway, what started as a gently gybe got completely out of hand, and this is what they do. Well, from time to time anyway. It’s great viewing, eh? Any second now (6) will get down on their knees and feign allegiance to their illustrious moral leader, and not long after that they’ll get in the car and drive home and shag their brains out. Categorically nothing to worry about. They’re fine.

Question: does (8) enjoy being lauded as some kind of living legend?
Mmmm….yes.
Does (6)?
Not so much.
Is (6) as capable of genius and success as (8)?
Yes.
Does (6) really believe that?
Mmmm….maybe yes maybe no, but it’s tough for them in the presence of you-know-who.
Does (6) handle confrontation as well as (8)?
No. No one does. 
Is (6) a loyal and wonderful supporter of (8)?
We think so, yes.
Can we same the same of (8)?
Believe it or not, but actually, yes. (8) is a tremendous supporter of (6) and probably their biggest fan.
The End.

For better or for worse, this is high-octane duo. (8) is a bar room brawler while (7) tends to spend their time actually standing on the bar leading a group chorus. Death-defying acts are therefore not really new concepts to either of them, and we suspect the greatest hurdle these two will face is to be able to carry on their merry way without offending the other too greatly. Will they succeed? We don’t know. We suspect no one does, not even these two. In which case, if you know them, get yourself a comfy seat, make sure you’re far enough away from the fire that you don’t get burnt, get yourself a big box of popcorn and enjoy the show.

Wow, how long is a piece of string? Could these two be amazing? Yep, without a doubt. Both love the spotlight and with (7)’s fun-loving modus operandi in concert with (8)’s outspoken sense of right and wrong, although they’re not bad at hunting pure fun themselves, they can do just about anything. As a couple they are supremely magnetic and there aren’t many people who don’t know of them, even if they don’t know them personally, but behind closed doors can be a tumultuous affair, and that’s only with the two of them in the room.

One of the pitfalls of this little pairing is that (7) always wants to feel like they have the ability to spread their wings and leap from a mountain top - at a moments notice, usually - whereas (8)’s plans are more thought out, which is commendable and necessary, but they rely heavily on being able to manipulate and/coerce those around them into helping. And if the timing isn’t right for (7) and (8) insists, then it will all go to shit in a second. (7) will resent being controlled and dictated to, and (8) will resent (7) being selfish, self-absorbed and non-compliant. Both parties have a case to answer in this instance.

These two have a fine time, although (7)’s relative lack of confrontational ability means they are, once in a while, not only offended by how (8) apparently treats them, but how (8) deals with others. From both perspectives there is something to be taken away here, potentially, and maybe this is why they were/are/should be together in the first place? Make no mistakes & learn no lessons, right? This is a mantra which holds true for each of us, it’s just that, for (7) and (8) the learning of the lesson will neither be quiet nor lengthy in duration. Let’s just see how it goes…

Like it or loathe it, (7) isn’t the team player (8) is. On top of this, (7) isn’t the bull-headed leader that (8) is, and they also occasionally resent being led by anyone, even though they sometimes need it. Yes, (8) knows this and attempts to urge and assist (7) as gently as possible without making them feel like they’re under personal attack, but this gentleness will only last for so long. Anyway, that sounds pretty gloomy, but we have a powerful couple here and the stakes are raised just a little bit when compared to normal. Certainly, the noise they make is louder than usual and we have no idea what will happen. Possibly neither do they, so you’re in the dark just as much as we are. Let’s just wish them all the best, eh?

Ever seen two elephant seals in full combat? It’s a loud, terrifying and bloody affair but rarely is anyone killed. Sure, egos might be dented briefly but, let’s face it, they each love the combat. When they’re in sync they have the potential to barnstorm any situation and achieve greatness, trusting they have a like-minded juggernaut standing next to them. Here in the real world, though, two leaders will undoubtedly, at some point, bang chests together and it won’t be in the bedroom, although that is probably a fun part of life for them, no matter how poorly they are getting on. In the end, there’s probably simply too much energy in the one room for two people to deal with.

Can you imagine Napoleon Bonaparte being married, not to Marie Antoinette, but to Napoleon Bonaparte? That’s right, neither can we, but by jingoes they’ll get a lot done while they’re together and make some kind of reputation for themselves. That part at least will a resounding success. The rest will be a disaster and many soldiers will die for no apparent reason whatsoever.

We’ve got it - a new craze which we think will be hugely popular at the speedway. What we’ll do is get two giant, super-charged semi-trailers, fill them both with fireworks, line them up at either end of the track then get them to drive at each other and collide head-on in front of the grandstand. We’ll time the fireworks to go off remotely, just before impact. What do you think? People will come for miles to watch this event, no question, and we’ll supply visors and ear muffs and small fire extinguishers. It’ll be great! Imagine the noise! Although, yes, there will be a bit of a mess to clean up, probably.

Cripes, have you ever gone and spent a few days at their house? Every single thing becomes a competition. Last night they wanted to watch different things on the tele’ and they had a full-on wrestling match in the living room. We think their kids must be used to it because they didn’t react at all. It went on for twenty minutes until the remote was accidentally tossed out the window, at which point it immediately started to rain. One of the kids fetched the remote from the front yard but the rain had killed it and there ensued a wrestle to see who was going to change stations on the TV manually, until they crashed into it and broke it. That’s when the kids started wailing, and that was it for us. We left and stayed at the caravan park.

These two are either magnificent or they are a train wreck. If they’re not on the same page and in sync with each other, they’ll whinge and spit and carry on, insisting that the other is a treacherous, lying wannabe. If they are, they’ll form a spectacularly powerful and capable couple who listen, advise and analyse, who communicate very clearly, and who could achieve literally anything they put their minds to. And there doesn’t seem like there is much middle ground. So, yes, good luckyou two, we hope you’re in sync and if you get to launch whatever it is you were talking about launching, we’d love an invite, as ever. Thank you, and farewell until then.

If we imagine (8) as a very powerful handgun, then (9) is the hand-crafted, velvet-lined case made especially for it. There is no doubt they are completely different people - (8) is loud and brash and in-your-face while (9) is calming and forgiving and warm - and so we expect they might compliment one another very nicely, and perhaps for a short while they will. If and when situations become problematic, however, and life does tend to toss the push bike into the bath on occasion, then this is where any complimentary notions are forgotten. (8) will want to raise hell, barge into the manager’s office no matter who is there and start tearing off wall paper with their bare teeth, while (9) will go very quiet and perhaps even turn invisible. Does this matter? Let’s find out…

Worst case scenario: The angry human, (8), storms in the door after a frustrating, miserable day at work to find the pet hound, (9), not where they usually are, bouncing around at the front door, elated to see their buddy (8), but sitting in the corner of the lounge room where they are refusing to make eye contact.  
“What have you done?” asks (8), sounding awfully grave.
“No, I haven’t done anything. Can’t we just be friends?” suggests (9)’s body language. “And please, don’t go into the kitchen.”
“Have you broken something in the kitchen (9)?” (8) asks. “Hmmmmm?”
At this, (9) scurries over to (8)’s feet and lavishes attention in the vain hope of preventing (9) from leaving the lounge room. And it’s all downhill from here folks.

These two make for a tantalising prospect. The engine room of the duo, (8), provides all the propulsion and energy for the vessel, where as (9) is a loving and attentive purser whose job is to ensure all the passengers are happy, and that they have everything they need. Storms aren’t things either they or the passengers love, while (8) on the other hand gets off on trying to smash through giant waves, the bigger the better, and they end up just getting angry if nothing seems to be happening. (9) loves the cruising life when the sun is out and when the bow is gently shooshing its way across a blue ocean so what to do? No one wants to go down at sea, and everyone is at least partly delighted to be sea worthy, but where is the delicious middle ground for these two?

Sometimes, it’s true. As much as they adore (8), and are inspired by their power and forcefulness, their never-say-die attitude and their tenacity in the face of pressure, (9) wishes, just once in a while, they would just shut the hell up and actually not insist that anyone do anything. And yes, the inverse is true, also. That is, while (8) loves (9)’s attention and appreciation, they often appear to be lacking the interest or the enthusiasm they expect and feel that they deserve. Most of all, they hate the fact that, rather than just say they don’t like something, (9) will simply change the topic altogether and totally shut down. Is it always like this? Of course not.

(8) is like a horse trainer who will do anything to win. Drugs, whippings, bribes - you name it. (9) on the other hand is just a lovely, contented horse - at least, they used to be contented - who loves running, loves the idea of a human on their back, and who wants to do well, but mostly, who just wants to eat nice grass and not necessarily get up every morning at three a.m. Especially when its freezing cold. Both of them appear to be trapped by the life they’re in, so, we’re not sure. Anyone have any suggestions?

A nice combo’. If the two of them were charged with running the company, then (1) would do the hard-nosed negotiating while (9) would ensure the employees were looked after and that the environment wasn’t being degraded too much. (9) doesn’t handle the high-powered situations like (1) and the only issue which might arise is how each of them handle the ramifications of this deep recession we’re apparently about to walk into. Having said that, they understand each other very well, including their different roles, and one would imagine that when hardship does arrive these two will ride with the punches together, laughing as they go and reminding each other of what’s important. Best of all, after coming out the back of such trials they’d be grateful they experienced it together. Splendid.

The quintessential good cop, bad cop. Good, being (9) and bad being (1), and they do their job very well. (9) is a wonderful second in charge, if you like, who has more kudos on the street in lieu of a friendlier, more engaging nature, and (1) is better at dealing with the intricacies of a case, and plotting a method to get the bad guy or fix the problem. They solve most cases they’re involved with and the Captain, back at headquarters, feels lucky to have them on board. And so do we.

(9) and (1)’s Funeral Service. Death Might Be Wonderful, is their motto. Not only do they both believe in some kind of afterlife, but they appreciate helping out here at the finish line, and to assist families through this difficult time. True, many families are a little put off by their stance but they seem to provide real care to those remaining, and the testimonies of these people are the proof in the pudding. (1) usually deals with the organisational running of the business -  schedules, embalming rosters, hearse maintenance, etc - while (9)’s role is almost purely interpersonal. They radiate warmth and compassion even when they’re alone in the bathroom, so you can only imagine how wonderful they are at consoling grieving families. Yep, Death Might Be Wonderful is doing very well, and we expect that to continue. Bless.

Don’t you just love the corner store? And how long have (9) and (1) been running it for? Feels like forever. You can see (1) at sunrise if you’re up early enough, dragging in the newspapers and stacking up the daily milk arrivals. (9) doesn’t turn up until later, ever-ready with a smile and a bit of a yarn for whoever walks in the door. (1) deals with the books, ordering stock and all the admin, and they always keeps an eye on customers when they’re out the back, just in case (9) is too busy chatting to someone to notice one of the young kiddies stealing a chocolate bar, which happens occasionally. Little does (1) know, however, that (9) is actually very aware of everything, it’s just that they think it’s rather cute and, importantly, they believe a little theiving probably teaches kids about daring and deftness of hand. Anyway, the store is going very well and the town loves them both.

The hard-nosed reporter, (1), and the travel-weary camera person, (9), have been a great team for a while now and we don’t expect that to change. (1) always has an idea about the kind of story they want to create and (9)’s advice is vital - they’ve had far more experience on the street dealing with idiotic strangers, they're better at helping people relax, let alone setting up the best lighting. On the flipside (9) never needs to suggest anything to (1) in terms of which questions to ask because they have those specifics sussed. Better than that, (1) isn’t an arrogant twat like some reporters (9) has dealth with. They’re very happy to help setting up and, overall, they just enjoy each other's company. Actually, they’re on TV right now.

Perhaps (2) and (9) were siblings, or mother and daughter or something, in a past life? It’s like a yogi master going out with a Zen Buddhist. With so much warmth, generosity and consideration in the room it’s difficult to imagine either of them raising their voice over anything. “Are they telepathic?” is a question many friends ask of them. These same friends also presume they either sleep or meditate a lot because of how utterly serene they always appear to be. In any case, maybe that’s the problem, if/when there ever is one? Surely, some time, at least one of them needs to feel the wind rushing through their metaphorical hair. And what happens then? Having said all that, these two are possibly ideal for each other.

These two should open up a clinic. They could call it, The Just Come Around And Hang Out At Our Place And You’ll Soon Feel Great No Matter What Centre. They probably wouldn’t even charge you, or maybe have a donations box out the front. In a nutshell, these two are good for each other and good for the world. Sure, (2) is the more outgoing of the duo and (9) has a more calming aspect, which both (2) and the world at large appreciates, but there isn’t much going on here which isn’t appreciated. So, we’ll let them go about their rather splendid business while we go about ours. Not much to be worried about here, kids.

What do you get when you put two rather lovely optimists together? You get a great big fluffy happy cake that everyone adores, and that very few people get sick of. Indeed, the only ones who wont like the cake are those classically cynical or antagonistic types who get off on confrontation for the hell of it. Well booo hooo to them!

One imagines Doctor (9) accidentally being seated next to Nurse (2) on the plane, for their flight to Africa, and would any of us be surprised to learn that they’re about to spend the next six months working side by side at the same refuge camp in the Democratic Republic of Congo? In all likelihood, the rest may very well be history, and you definitely don’t need to hear why these two are well suited from us. Equally, don’t ask them. They’ll just get embarrassed, especially (9).

It’s not that these two are interchangeable, but, you know, they could be. Both of them are compassionate and caring souls who tend to make the world a better place, collectively and individually, and the only real hiccup arrives when a hard decision has to be made by someone. Maybe the dog needs to be put down, or maybe there is a grandmother somewhere who is asking to be euthanised? Sounds ridiculous, but life throws up these scenarios and they have to be confronted sooner or later, so, how will these two go? (Actually, we suspect they’ll go very well, but it’ll still be interesting to see how they, or someone, deals with it. Until then though, it’s happy sailing.)

It’s as if we’re watching a sitcom. The high-powered, fretting fool, (3), trots out the door to work with humble aspirations of being incredibly industrious, generally dazzling, semi-famous and perhaps even world-changing. Later in the day they arrive home stressed and bothered, which is where our host of the century, (9), gets to tend our strident wannabe. Luckily, at home, they desire similar things in life and, yes, (9) admires (3)’s world conquering attitude, but don’t worry, this isn’t all one-way traffic. (3) admires (9)’s capacity to remain calm and their skill at producing a constant, warm interaction because they know they need the help. They might do okay, these two.

Now we’re talking. The potent bulldozer (3) in concert with the gentle and loving landscaper (9), who darts around them with daisies in their hair, removing vulnerable animals, offering water and sandwiches to the bulldozer driver, and generally making sure no one and nothing is being accidentally run over and/or killed. And (9) also takes photographs of (3)’s wonderful work so they can post them on social media later, because (3) secretly loves the adulation. Yes, it’s a little asinine for (3) to need this but so what, no one is perfect although these two aren’t far off it.

What do you get when you cross a potent leader and general go-getter, (3), with lovely warm magical glove, (9), who imparts the wearer with serene superpowers of optimism, loveliness and serenity? That’s right, you get the most wonderful and stress-free ride down the mountain side, that is so fun and tremendous you can’t really imagine doing anything else for the rest of the day. The End.

It’s not that (9) is lazy, it’s just that they operate on a slower tic, and so (3) can always help them get parts of their life in order, if indeed they require any of that. Maybe (9) needs their tax receipts organised? Maybe they even need to learn why or how keeping tax receipts is theoretically important in the first place? Anyway, as silly as some of these concepts are to (9) in the grand scheme of things, (3) is a diligent and competent cat who grasps most administrative systems very well, and who enjoys helping out when they have a few minutes free. Ditto, (9) might just help (3) relax and to appreciate the finer things in life which money can rarely buy.

Ain’t no car wrecks here folks. No smashed vases thrown against a kitchen wall. No divots above the TV where a high velocity potato has met its doom. No sugar-filled petrol tanks in anyone’s car. These two are a nice mix of power and pragmatism, as displayed by (3), and stability, humility and calm, as exemplified by (9). So only a couple of questions remain: are they getting married, and are you invited?

Respectively, (4) and (9) are on a fervent search for that soul mate who they feel ‘completes them’. Is that a corny load of unmitigated bullshit?… probably, but as it stands they might be on the right track. They’re definitely more likely to lounge around all day together rather than leap out of bed at dawn, don the matching lycra and hit the running track or the freezing beach swim. Fluffy pillows, tea and toast in bed, big long talks and gentle caresses are what’s on offer here ladies and gentlemen. 
Bored yet? They probably feed each other in restaurants, who knows. But, perhaps that lack of pure energy is what irks them in the end, if it happens.

No, we’re not in the presence of two professional pole dancers, but two professional bird-watchers who, in a perfect world, get to enjoy their ornithological pursuits while at the same time rubbing shoulders with each other. One might argue that it’s not even the birds they’re interested in, but the necessarily quiet and peaceful places they have to hide together while they list down, and occasionally photograph, their quarry. And they get to whisper to each other, which they like doing as well. Yep, it’s all good for these two.

Yes, another loving, romantic soup in the brewing here kiddies, and why not indeed! Both crave that intimate connection where feelings are shared, partners are encouraged and acts of romance are commonplace. Nice work if you can get it, right? On a bad day (9) will shut up shop and not feel like talking about anything, which has a tendency to really piss (4) off, where as (9) might be bothered by (4)’s absurd mood swings, although we suspect this is a rarity more than the norm. Shall we all take a seat and just see how they get on?….Wonderful.

Does (4) provide enough oomph for (9), and does (9) allow and encourage (4) to express themselves fully? The answer, most of the time, is a resounding yes. Maybe it's the artistic, emotional streak they both share - we don’t know, but we like it. Are they shagging much, does anyone know?….Anyway, we look forward to the update ladies and gentlemen and unless there is some major disaster or other, you probably won’t see these two for a while, such is their propensity for lazing all over each other in front of Netflix.

What? A renegade couple deliberately crashed a car into the local ATM, shot two police officers and high-tailed it across the border? Well good on them, but in a billion, actually, in ten billion years you are never going to see (4) and (9) do that. Hell, the only time these two move quickly is to dash for the kitchen after the microwave beeps to let them know their hot chocolates are ready, and they’re not shy on the cocoa sprinkled on top, either. Somehow it makes their little cubby hut that they have going in the lounge room more romantic. Yeah, I know, we don’t get it either. We’ve stopped asking, but so what, they’re happy and that’s what counts.

“Shoosh, quiet please. This is a library and as you can see people are busy studying, working and preparing, as well as fitting-in with their surroundings as much as possible. What? Music? Shit no, no music. Well, only earplugs but even then make sure it’s not too loud. You’re permitted to make a coffee - just follow (9), one of our very attentive librarians over there. They’ll show you how, and they’re very friendly. Oh, and you want to know if anyone has fun in here? Well, of course they do. Look at that researcher, just here. That's (5) and they're here every day - reading up on the nature of the universe, we think. The only person they speak to is (9) and (9) assures us that, despite the frowns of concentration, (5) couldn’t be happier.” 
So, anyone up for a library visit?

Should these two be together? It’s a question their respective friends have been discussing amongst themselves behind their backs for months now. Lord knows, if they’re going to they’ll need their friends’ help in setting up some kind of contrived scenario, because (9) and (5) appear to spend too much time naval gazing, or staring into text books and self-help guides, respectively. It depends. So, presuming that does happen, and their peers help get them together, can we hope for a little greatness? Well, yes, you can lead a horse to water but you can’t make it drink, but in this case, oddly enough, and against the apparent odds, these two might do okay. Let’s just wait and see, shall we?…

Can (5) handle the emotional spectrum of (9)? 
Yep, we think so. 
Can (9) handle the aloof, almost analytical nature of (5)? 
Yes, probably, on the proviso (5) is, as is typically the case, interested in new ideas and is thoughtful and constructive with their responses. 
Are they good in bed? 
Dunno, check their sexual compatibility - not our business. 
Do they laugh?
Ummm, yes. Often, actually, although in a strange way neither of them, in hindsight, can actually pinpoint anything the other says as being particularly funny. Weird eh? 
Anyway, they’ll work it out.

Don't let the 60% put you off. These two are better suited to each other than they realise. Yes, there are philosophical and emotional differences, mostly in how they think and express themselves, and yes, while you may laugh that this is just about everything, there is actually quite a compassionate and close kind of vibe between them. Now, yes, we know (5), you detest that word almost as much as (9) appreciates it, but you know what we’re talking about here don’t you? There is a ‘vibe’, so pretend to ignore it as much as you like. Anyway, we’d suggest plonking these two in a big baking tray, dose them in a layer of time, cover them with nice cold sections of raw, silly humour, let them simmer under the heat of some gentle sexual curiosity, and let them stew in each others’ juices for a while. Amen.

If (5) is the bank robber who has spent years mapping-out their escape path, recording security rosters at the bank, monitoring the quietest times in the street, obtaining and preparing a getaway car etc, then (9) is the usually-capable accomplice who, on the morning of the robbery, suddenly decides they don’t want to hold a gun anymore and would be far happier if they both brandished some kind of stick instead. Truth be known, (9) has been feeling like this for a while but, due to (5)’s steadfast dedication to the plan, and their apparent glee at how it was all panning out - and lord knows (5) doesn’t express glee that often - they felt too guilty about bringing it up. 
“So why now?” (5) asks, more perplexed than angry. 
“I don’t know. Guns just don't feel right.”
At which point, (5) plunges their head into their hands because there goes two years of planning down the drain. And (9)’s chances for some make-up sex later are very slim.

Common as muck, this type of couple. Why is that? Well, (6) wants to obey the laws of the land and ensure they never change their job or their eating habits while (9) is dead-keen on paying off their mortgage and attaining ‘independence’. Big Brother and the tax department loves these two, and you may have noticed that the television networks are trying to brainwash the population into thinking and behaving the same way. Anyway, when you meet them we can only suggest that you refrain from making any sudden movements or making loud, unexpected noises. They get easily startled and once you scare them off there’s no way they’ll come back in a hurry. Life is a surprising, chaotic beast to deal with, usually, and we wonder if this lack of capacity to deal with quick surprises has anything to do with a huge divorce rate? Be that as it may, we wish them all the best.

And here we have our proud and healthy horse, (6), with a tremendously shiny coat and well-polished hooves. Excellent. And here we have (9), our friendly, kind of dopey and extremely chilled-out donkey who doesn’t really mind too much about anything really, and whose sole job is to just kind of hang around in the paddock and keep (6) company, and to make them feel a little bit special. (6) enjoys being viewed as a lovely, potentially powerful and responsible individual, where as (9) loves chaff and the more carrots they receive in the morning the better. Are they a happy couple? Aaah, well, ignorance is bliss, true, but we’d say that usually, they’re doing okay. How’s that?

Do these two need a sea change? Should they just sell-up the whole thing and get a tiny little shack down the coast? Well, (6) likes the idea on paper and it was (9)’s in the first place, but the wheels of change take a long time to turn in some households and this one is no exception. But, they’ll talk about it for a long while until after a year or two or three of (9) being genuinely excited that they might finally get to live near the ocean, it seems (6) has finally bared their true feelings on the issue: Mental stimulation might be a tough for (6) with nothing to do other than buy organic veggies from beach-side markets and they never really like the idea of fishing in the first place. So, what to do? We know, come back in a year and find out. Amen.

If there is a wee problem beginning to develop with the car, (9) is more likely to take the attitude of ignoring it and hoping it just gets better, where as (6) will either try and determine exactly what the issue is, or find someone who will. One way or the other the problem is going to be fixed, and perhaps (9)’s role is to keep (6) motivated and happy while they go about their business? (9) is definitely not likely to fuss and worry, thereby getting in (6)’s face. Actually, (6) would probably appreciate a bit more of that from (9), but then they wouldn’t be (9). Anyway, in that regard they’re not a bad couple…..and maybe 50% slightly underestimates them?

Ever seen The Big Lebowski? (9), ‘The Dude’, and (6), ‘Walter’, love playing ten pin bowls but the means with which they each receive joy from the enterprise are quite different. Are they a good couple? Well, yes and no, and like everything in life there are good bits and bad. (9) is not so much lazy as they are ambivalent, and (6), while entertaining and obviously intelligent, is a little wound-up. It’s certainly entertaining to watch. Let us know how they get on.

Firefighters exist because of these two. The natural prankster in (7) has a natural fixer in (9) and both tend to be glass-is-half-full kind of people. Better than that, (9) encourages (7) to at least save a little money for a rainy day, whereas (7) encourages (9) to visit the sex shop, just for the hell of it, once in a while.
However, neither are very good at dealing with stress or confrontational discussions, and at some point these moments inevitably arrive. So long as the sun is out, they avoid living anywhere near a Middle Eastern trouble spot and fresh water comes out of the tap after they turn it on, they’ll do very well.

Once again, an outstanding performance from these two. The both of them fairly float over the rink as if their skates aren’t even actually touching the ice. (7)’s melodramatic expressions as they hurl the perfectly serene (9) into the air repeatedly are, themselves, something to behold. And how (9) seems to remain so calm, that high in the air, is beyond us. Complete confidence is a must for these moves, and it’s clearly visible with these two. And did you see that last one? (9) seemed to give (7) a little wink in the slow-mo, who immediately dug their skates in before the two pirouetted out through the air, locked together as one! HOW DID THEY DO THAT! THE CROWDS GOING NUTS, AND SO ARE WE!

Did you hear how these two got together?

(7) spotted (9) across the room, who at the time was leaning against the bar in the middle of their friends, having just told some joke that had everyone chuckling. Even the bartender. 
(7) sauntered over, checked their fabulous reflection in one of the mirrors on their way there, and excused themselves as they barged into the group.
Silently, (7) pointed their finger at (9) with a grin that was cast somewhere between cheeky and knowing. 
“You. Me,” (7) said. “Let’s go.”
(9) let out a big sigh, dropped their head in mock disappointment, put their drink on the bar and said, “Okay.”
The end.

These two can entertain themselves for hours by doing seemingly very little. They find beauty and comedy in the smallest things, they encourage weird ideas in each other, the weirder the better, and they enjoy watching their partners operate and the effect they have on others. (9) is softer and subtler in their approach than (7), to just about everything, and when times are good they appreciate the differences, even endeavouring to remember to try these different approaches out. For instance, (7) will attempt to be a little more subdued sometimes, just as (9) might even attempt being a little bit grandiose. The only hitch arises here when emotional disaster strikes because both of them would prefer to run to the hills than stop and face the dilemma head on.

We always hope a couple is great in bed, but with these two it probably doesn’t even matter. If (7) is the dancing clown then (9) is the appreciative spectator and part-time assistant. Embarrassing hiccups are forgotten about quickly, painful people and situations are dismissed from their lives even faster than that and at social events they sometimes discover people accidentally milling around them. Yep, these two are potentially that good. We’ll leave it at that.

If and when situations become problematic, however, and life does tend to toss the push bike into the bath on occasion, then this is where any complimentary notions are forgotten. (8) will want to raise hell, barge into the manager’s office no matter who is there and start tearing off wall paper with their bare teeth, while (9) will go very quiet and perhaps even turn invisible. Does this matter? Let’s find out…

“What have you done?” asks (8), sounding awfully grave.
“No, I haven’t done anything. Can’t we just be friends?” suggests (9)’s body language. “And please, don’t go into the kitchen.”
“Have you broken something in the kitchen (9)?” (8) asks. “Hmmmmm?”
At this, (9) scurries over to (8)’s feet and lavishes attention in the vain hope of preventing (9) from leaving the lounge room. And it’s all downhill from here folks.

(8) is like a horse trainer who will do anything to win. Drugs, whippings, bribes - you name it. Question: 
What do you get when you put two, soft, delicious, succulent cream pies together?
Answer: 
(a) potential, gluttonous perfection.
(b) a fat gut, a lack of energy, a lack of decision-making, a lack of mental agility and an overall lack of health and happiness.
…Correct, but mostly (b). 
As a couple these two are not as dire as we suggest, but only to a point. Yes, there is time and no one is rushed here. Both parties appreciate the other and everyone is friendly - to each other and the world at large - but are they too chilled-out for their own good? They might even become so inert that they don’t even bother bringing up issues for fear of rocking the boat. Are they passive aggressive in the end? Who knows? We suggest you both look for more of a challenge!

My god, it’s like watching a Laurel and Hardy skit, where both of them are walking into a restaurant.
